title: Claude Code stream-json messages (Claude Code 2.1.311)
$comment: For each message type the CLI writes (<type>[_<subtype>]Output) and reads (<type>Input) in stream-json mode. Generated from Claude Code 2.1.311 by calling the zod v4 toJSONSchema embedded in the binary on its own validator (method A, runtime export). Anchor: the SDK schema module, unions described as "Everything the CLI writes to its output stream" and "Everything a client may write to the CLI's input stream". Do not edit by hand: run "bun run schemas".

active_goalOutput.description: Emitted when the user's /goal Stop hook reports met (clears) or not-yet-met (bumps iterations + last_reason). Any surface with a goal indicator re-renders from this. value is null when the goal is cleared. From internal QueryEvent 'active_goal'.

citations.description: Citation locations backing the text, as the API defines them.

input.description: The tool's input object; its shape is the named tool's input schema.

caller.description: Which caller invoked the tool (direct, or a server tool), when reported.

items.description: A response content block. text, tool_use and thinking blocks are modelled; the other API block types (server tool use and results, MCP tool blocks, container_upload, compaction, ...) are accepted by type tag only, and consumers must tolerate types newer than this list.

stop_reason.description: end_turn, max_tokens, stop_sequence, tool_use, pause_turn, refusal, ...; null while the message is still streaming.

stop_details.description: Structured refusal details, when stop_reason is refusal.

container.description: The code-execution container used by the request, if any.

context_management.description: Context-management edits applied during the request, if any.

message.description: Shaped like an Anthropic Messages API Message object (role "assistant"): id, model, content blocks (text, thinking, tool_use, ...), stop_reason and usage. When streamed, content typically holds the single block this message delivers and stop_reason is still null — see SDKAssistantMessage. See the Messages API reference for the block types.

historical.description: @internal Replayed history rather than a live message (stamped by the Remote Control bridge when it flushes history to the session server).

refused_message_id.description: @internal Only on the assistant message that reports a refusal: the API msg_* id of the refused response (message.id on this message is a local UUID). Absent when the CLI has no well-formed id for it.

user_message_uuid.description: Client uuid of the user message this turn is answering (submitMessage options.uuid), stamped on an assistant message each time that send changes — the turn's FIRST top-level assistant message (which may carry only a thinking block, or be a synthetic API-error message), and then, for a turn started by a synthetic (meta) prompt, the first assistant message after each queued user message folded in mid-turn (the fold takes the echo over); with --include-partial-messages the turn's first non-ping stream event is stamped too, independently (see SDKPartialAssistantMessage), so the same uuid may appear on both — either binds the reply to the send it answers without waiting for the result; the server keeps the first stamp it sees per uuid. A turn started by a typed prompt keeps that uuid for its whole turn, so it stamps once per frame kind. A meta turn's own uuid is stamped only when the host vouches it is the client event's own (on a hosted session, the uuid the session server persisted: delivered content such as a Slack owner ping, a Slack-bot observation or a client-injected synthetic turn), never for a prompt the CLI minted itself — except that a turn carrying resume_reason, such as the boot-time rescue turn re-running a turn a worker restart interrupted mid-way, stamps the interrupted turn's own last user prompt, the send it answers, where that can be vouched for (a turn that goes on from a permission answer or from in-flight tool calls may first re-send, unstamped, the assistant message that made those calls); either way a user message folded into a meta turn takes the echo over from it (the rescue turn absorbing messages sent while the session was down; a bot-observation turn absorbing a human's post), and the first reply frame of each kind after that fold carries the folded message's uuid — the first reply that message got. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content` — so it is not replayed to the model. Absent on every other frame of the turn, on subagent frames (parent_tool_use_id set), on turns that neither had a client uuid nor folded a user message in, and from older producers.

user_message_uuids.description: Client uuids of every user message whose prompt this turn has consumed so far, in consumption order — all members of a prompt batch the host merged into this one turn (several messages sent close together run as one turn whose user_message_uuid is the LAST member's), then any user message folded into the turn before this frame — so a consumer that sent any of them can bind this reply to its own send by finding its uuid anywhere in the list. Always contains user_message_uuid; at most 64 entries. Present exactly when user_message_uuid is, on the same frames; absent from older producers (fall back to user_message_uuid).

resume_reason.description: Why this frame's turn continues one that a worker restart interrupted. Such a turn is the automatic re-run of the interrupted turn (CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN), or one that goes on from the answer to the permission prompt the new worker took over, or from that turn's tool calls still in flight. The value is the host's CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_REASON when it set one (host_draining, checkpoint_restore, container_recreated, …), else 'interrupted_turn'. Stamped on the same reply frames as user_message_uuid (which on such a turn names the interrupted turn's own last user prompt), so a consumer can tell its first reply from the interrupted attempt's. Absent on every other turn (also one that goes on from the answer to any other permission prompt), on thinking_tokens frames, and from older producers.

resumed_from_incomplete_thinking.description: This turn continued the preceding truncated assistant turn inside its trailing signed thinking block (max-output-tokens recovery). Its thinking signatures are cumulative over that preceding thinking-only turn, so a history replayed through the bridge must carry this flag back for the normalizer to keep the run's prefix on the wire. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content` — so it is not replayed to the model.

supersedes.description: Wire uuids of previously-delivered messages that this message replaces (refusal-fallback supersede). The list can include tombstoned tool_result frames from the refused leg, not only assistant frames. Evict the named messages on arrival and treat this frame as their canonical replacement. Idempotent with the end-of-turn model_refusal_fallback notice, whose retracted_message_uuids remains the complete audit record for the turn.

aborted.description: True when this assistant message was truncated by an interrupt/abort before the stream completed: stop_reason was never received and the content may end mid-word. Absent on normally completed messages.

agent_id.description: ID of the subagent that produced this message: the `task_id` of its task events, unchanged when the subagent is resumed. Absent on main-thread messages.

subagent_type.description: Subagent type that produced this message.

task_description.description: Description of the subagent task that produced this message.

tool_use_meta.description: @internal Display metadata for this message's tool_use blocks, keyed by block id. display_name is the MCP server's `tool.annotations.title` when provided, otherwise a readable transform of the wire name; server_display_name is the MCP server's own display name; icon_url is the MCP server's directory icon URL (claude.ai connectors only); server_id is the mcpsrv_ connector id of a server provisioned by claude.ai, set by the CLI from claude.ai's own connector listing, so a client may show the call as that connector's. server_id_stamp is the X-MCP-Server-ID header value, lower-cased, of an http entry in the dynamic scope (passed in at launch or by a later mcp_set_servers push). Claude Code Remote writes the connector's uuid there when the session has one, otherwise an id it generates; the CLI checks only its shape (at most 128 characters of letters, digits, '.', '_', ':' and '-'; anything else yields no stamp), not whose it is, since a --mcp-config or SDK-host entry can write anything. A client may look it up in its own server list, treat a miss as a server it does not know (never as an error), and show a hit as the entry's claim to be that server, not as proof. They are separate fields: a server provisioned by claude.ai carries server_id, a dynamic-scope http entry server_id_stamp. Both absent for a plugin's, a repo's, a settings or an agent entry. Neither is a permission grant. tool_name is the tool's name as its server lists it, without the mcp__<server>__ prefix. Omitted for blocks whose display label equals the wire name (built-in tools). Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content` — so it is not replayed to the model.

narration_block_indexes.description: @internal Ascending zero-based indexes into this frame's `message.content` of the thinking blocks whose signature the server tagged block_kind 'narration' (server summaries of the prose between tool calls, not the model's own reasoning), so a renderer can label them as summaries without decoding the signature envelope. Fail-closed: an unparseable or legacy signature is not listed. A listed block can have empty thinking text when the request returned no thinking text; give those ordinary thinking treatment. Omitted when the frame has no such block, and by CLI versions before this field existed; treat unlisted thinking blocks as ordinary thinking. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content` — so it is not replayed to the model.

narration_hint.description: @internal Display-only, for this frame's narration_block_indexes blocks: how to draw their trailing ' · summarized' hint, by the same rule Claude Code's terminal UI uses for the model that produced the frame. 'hidden': draw no hint. 'faint': draw ' · summary'. Omitted: draw ' · summarized'. Sent only to the VS Code extension and only on frames that have such a block; older CLI versions never send it. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content` — so it is not replayed to the model.

thinking_duration_ms.description: @internal How long the thinking block in this frame took to stream, in whole milliseconds (at least 1): from its content_block_start to its content_block_stop, so the wait for the response's first token is not counted. For display only. Sent only on a frame whose one content block is a thinking block that was streamed. Older CLI versions never send it, and a CLI that rebuilt its history from SDK frames does not send it when it replays that history, so be ready to show the block without a duration. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content` — so it is not replayed to the model.

thinking_display.description: @internal The thinking.display that Claude Code put in the API request body for the response that streamed this frame's thinking block. It has the same source and meaning as `thinking_display` on a stream event. Sent only on a frame whose one content block is a thinking block that was streamed, and only when the body had a display. Older CLI versions never send it, and a CLI that rebuilt its history from SDK frames does not send it when it replays that history. An absent key states nothing. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content` — so it is not replayed to the model.

timestamp.description: ISO timestamp of when this content block finished on the originating process. One API assistant turn may produce several assistant messages sharing a message.id, each with its own timestamp. Uses the originating host's clock, so it's for display only; do not order messages by this field. Older emitters omit it; consumers should fall back to receive time.

is_meta.description: @internal True when the message was synthesized by the loop (not a model response).

model.description: Main-loop model the usage was computed for.

total_tokens.description: Estimated tokens in use, unclamped — may exceed raw_max_tokens when over limit.

raw_max_tokens.description: The window usage is measured against: the resolved autocompact window — the model's believed limit, or a smaller compaction-policy window (a configured value, or e.g. the 200K boundary on 1M-window models).

over_limit.description: Present when total_tokens exceeds raw_max_tokens. kind says how the window was resolved, not whether the API will accept the next request: 'hard_limit' means the window is the model's believed limit (the API will refuse past it); 'compaction_window' means a compaction-policy window, which may or may not coincide with the model's hard limit.

name.description: Display name of the row as the CLI renders it, e.g. "Messages" or "MCP tools (deferred)". Use `kind` (not this name) to classify the row.

kind.description: What the row is: 'used' content occupies the window; 'free' is the remaining window; 'buffer' is the compaction reserve (autocompact or manual); 'deferred' rows are out-of-window tool schemas — listed for awareness, excluded from usage math.

items.description: One row of the /context usage-by-category breakdown. Rows may carry zero tokens; renderers typically hide those.

type.description: Display label of the memory-file source, e.g. "Project" or "User".

source.description: Raw source identifier, e.g. 'projectSettings', 'userSettings', 'plugin'. Built-in agents are excluded by the producer. Display labels are the renderer's concern.
Raw source identifier, e.g. 'userSettings', 'plugin', 'syncedSkills'.

skills.description: Omitted when no skills contribute tokens.

context_usage.description: Structured twin of the /context report, carried on the synthetic assistant message that delivers the markdown table. Present only on /context results from CLIs new enough to attach it; the markdown in message.content remains the canonical fallback. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content` — so it is not replayed to the model.

session.description: Cost and usage accumulated by the current session.

kind.description: The server's meter kind, e.g. 'session', 'weekly_all' or 'weekly_scoped'. Classify a row on this, never on a label.

group.description: The server's row group, e.g. 'session' or 'weekly'; rows render grouped under it, in the server's order.

resets_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the window resets.

scope.description: What a scoped row is for, a model or a surface, with the server's display label.

severity.description: The server's reading of the row for a meter's colour, e.g. 'normal', 'warning' or 'critical'. Every row here is the server's, so a client never grades a row itself.

is_active.description: The server's headline pick: the row a single-value indicator shows.

limits.description: The server's usage rows (the usage endpoint's limits[]), as sent: which meters apply, their scope, labels, severity and order are the server's, so a client renders them verbatim and a new meter needs no client release. Empty when the server reported no meters; null when the body carried no rows at all (a server that predates them). Null too while the usage fetch is failing: the rows here are only ever the server's current reply, so neither the row the CLI builds from rate-limit response headers for its own screen nor its snapshot of an earlier reply appears here.

extra_usage.description: Extra-usage (overage) spend for the billing period, when the plan has it. Amounts are in minor units of `currency` (cents for USD); is_enabled is false while extra usage cannot cover sends.

rate_limits.description: The plan's usage rows and extra-usage spend from the claude.ai usage endpoint; null when the CLI could not fetch them (no plan on this lane, or a token without the profile scope).

usage_report.description: Structured twin of the /usage report, carried on the synthetic assistant message that delivers its text: the session totals, the plan's usage rows and extra-usage spend, for remote clients that render a card from data. Present only on /usage results from CLIs new enough to attach it and from claude.ai-subscriber sessions; the text in message.content remains the canonical fallback. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content` — so it is not replayed to the model.

local_command_source.description: @internal The originating system local_command row's wire-form content (escaped frames), carried on the loop-synthesized local-command twin. Round-tripped so toInternalMessages rebuilds the internal system row on a bridge/SDK history replay — replay then matches the live session, where that row is model-visible — instead of dropping the output or replaying the twin's decoded display text. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content`.

local_command_run.description: @internal On the local-command twin, the run that printed the row: the command's name as `command.run` carried it (no slash), its arguments as the echo shows them (`***` when the command marks them sensitive) and, for a command a plugin registered, that plugin's name, or, for a row whose text plugins' `command.run` hooks answered or retold, the names the text is led by (untrusted text; absent for the binary's own command in its own words). Present when a `local` command's dispatch printed the row or a `command.run` hook answered it, absent on a never-ran notice. A surface that draws the hooks engine's `CommandOutput` site asks ui_render with these, the twin's text and its uuid as instance_id; toInternalMessages round-trips it onto the rebuilt row. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content`.

suggestion.description: unknown: the registered command closest to the typed name, no slash.

local_command_outcome.description: @internal On the local-command twin, what the row reports, so a host can offer a fix instead of relaying the text: 'unavailable_headless' (an interactive-panel command this session cannot open), 'unknown' (no command has the typed name), 'failed' (the command ran and failed), 'restart_required' (the change applies after Claude Code restarts). Absent when the row reports none of these; new kinds are additive, so treat an unknown one as absent. toInternalMessages round-trips it onto the rebuilt row. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content`.

is_virtual.description: @internal Display-only: rendered in the UI but filtered before API send.

batch_tool_uses.description: @internal `{id, name}` of the original Batch* tool_use block(s) for a message whose content was decomposed into synthetic v1 tool_use blocks. Round-tripped so a replayed history reassembles the batch block on the wire (not N synthetics). Input is reassembled from the synthetics in `message.content` — never carried here. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content` — so it is not replayed to the model.

wire_tool_inputs.description: @internal `tool_use.input` exactly as the API produced it, keyed by tool_use id, for a message whose `message.content` carries the client-normalized input. Round-tripped so a replayed history echoes each earlier tool call back to the API as the API emitted it (the server may hold its own copy of the turn). Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content`.

wire_ingest_context.description: @internal What the client-side input normalization read from process state (the working directory a leading `cd` was stripped against, the stamp applied to a Slack send) for the inputs in `wire_tool_inputs`, keyed by the same tool_use ids. Round-tripped with `wire_tool_inputs` so a replayed history can verify each recorded input against the normalized one exactly. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content`.

is_api_error_message.description: @internal True when this assistant message wraps an API error (from internal AssistantMessage.isApiErrorMessage).

api_error_status.description: @internal HTTP status code of the API error when is_api_error_message is true.

api_error_params.description: @internal Parameters of api_error, present only for the kinds that have any. effort: the effort level the API refused (effort_requires_thinking). media (media_removed): the kind of block the API refused; absent for media_budget. media_reason (media_removed): unsupported_by_model — the API said that the model does not accept PDF documents; media_budget — the request's images and documents together exceed the API's limit, and the requests that follow may leave out blocks of either kind; unprocessable — every other refusal, a gateway's report of a model's refusal among them. provider: the API provider whose credentials failed (provider_credentials, gateway_session_expired). remedy (provider_credentials, gateway_session_expired): refresh_command — a configured refresh command (awsAuthRefresh / gcpAuthRefresh) refreshes the credentials; refresh_credentials — refresh the provider's credentials by hand, no command is configured; adc — refresh the Google application default credentials or the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS key file; gateway_token — replace the gateway token supplied through ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS; host_managed — the host application owns these credentials; model_access — the credentials work but the model is not enabled for this account and region (Amazon Bedrock). rate_limit_info (usage_limit_reached): what the refused request's own response said about the limit, in the shape rate_limit_event carries. It is read from the same values as the message text, so its status, limit and reset are the text's: status is rejected and isUsingOverage false, rateLimitType names the limit, resetsAt is when it resets, and overageStatus, overageResetsAt, overageDisabledReason and limitScope say whose spend cap it is (the person's own cap arrives as org_level_disabled_until, as on rate_limit_event); no other member is sent. It is that refusal's record and is never updated, so compare resetsAt with the clock before calling the limit current.

api_error_code.description: @internal The server's error.details.error_code for this API error, copied through when it is an identifier (^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$) and dropped otherwise. Carries server gate codes this build has no api_error value for, so a host can key on a new gate without a Claude Code release. Absent when the response carried no code.

api_error_origin.description: @internal first_party when this API error was built from a response Anthropic's own API sent: the request used the firstParty provider, went to https://api.anthropic.com on the default port and was answered from there, not redirected, over TLS verified with no added CA (NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS), no verification override and no unix-socket tunnel. Absent in every other case: an ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL or WIF base_url override, a gateway, a third-party provider, a connection error, an error Claude Code raised itself, and any frame replayed from the transcript, SDK input or a remote session. Treat absence as unknown origin. It says which endpoint answered, not that the message text is the server's verbatim, and a CA installed in the system trust store can still intercept. An invalid-request message (400 or 422) can quote request values, so it is stamped only when it is one of the known Anthropic wordings, and no message is stamped that quotes the request's model id; render stamped text as plain text. New values may be added; treat an unknown value as absent.

error_details.description: @internal Raw API error message — preserves details (e.g. prompt-too-long token counts) that user-facing content discards.

advisor_model.description: @internal Advisor model that produced this message, when applicable.

attribution_agent.description: @internal Attribution stamp: agent name parsed from querySource (see messageAttribution.ts). May overlap with subagent_type.

attribution_mcp_server.description: @internal MCP server that produced this message.

attribution_mcp_tool.description: @internal MCP tool that produced this message.

assistantOutput.description: An assistant message. While a response streams the CLI emits one assistant message per completed content block, so several consecutive assistant messages can share message.id and each carries just that block in message.content; on those, message.stop_reason is null and message.usage is not final — the turn's stop reason and total usage arrive on the result message. parent_tool_use_id is non-null when the message was produced inside a subagent started by that tool_use.

enabled.description: Whether auto-compact is enabled on the worker (autoCompactEnabled setting + DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT / DISABLE_COMPACT env; DISABLE_COMPACT also disables manual /compact).

effective_window.description: The worker's resolved auto-compact window in tokens — resolveAutoCompactWindow output clamped to the model window, honoring /autocompact, CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW, clientdata and experiment overrides.

threshold.description: The token count where threshold-triggered compaction fires on the worker — effective_window minus the summary buffer, lowered further by CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE when set.

enforced.description: Whether threshold-triggered compaction will actually fire at `threshold`. False when the worker defers to the API's prompt-too-long (reactive mode) or context collapse owns headroom — clients then show % of window used instead of a countdown to a compaction that won't happen.

source.description: Which input decided the window (resolveAutoCompactWindow precedence order).

autocompact_stateOutput.description: @internal Worker-resolved auto-compact state, emitted by CCR workers at boot, whenever the resolved state changes (/autocompact, model switch, settings change), re-checked at each turn start, and re-emitted after a conversation reset. Thin clients adopt it so the "% until auto-compact" indicator counts down to the worker's real compaction trigger instead of re-resolving against client-local state. Turn-scoped divergence is accepted: a turn running under a skill/command frontmatter model override compacts against that model's window while the frame keeps the resting model's (the local indicator shares this limitation). From sessionState.onAutocompactInputsChanged.

command.description: Shell command run verbatim, without the model and without permission checks. Trust model matches the local TUI `!cmd` path (no sandbox, no per-command prompt). By default it runs in a one-shot `/bin/sh -c` (or `pwsh`) beside the conversation, which never sees it; on a cloud worker with tengu_cloud_session_shell on it runs as the TUI's `!cmd` does, through the Bash tool (its working directory carries over to later commands and to the model's Bash calls), as a turn of its own, so the model sees the command and its output. The worker refuses some commands with a row saying why (for example a stale one, one over 65,536 characters, one containing control characters, or one sent to a host that does not run them) and skips a duplicate silently (cli/headlessHost/bashCommand.ts).

cwd.description: Working directory for the command. Falls back to the session cwd when omitted. With tengu_cloud_session_shell on, the command runs in the session's current directory and one naming any other directory is refused.

bash_commandInput.description: @internal A user-initiated shell command. Input-only — sent by CCR clients that surface a dedicated terminal UI; never emitted on stdout. Acknowledged on arrival and, unless blank, too long or a duplicate, echoed at once as a `<bash-input>` replay row; then answered with exactly one more row: its output (a replay frame when run beside the conversation; a plain user message after its own turn when it joins the conversation, possibly followed by the model replying) or a `<bash-stderr>Not run: …</bash-stderr>` replay row saying why it was refused or dropped. A blank or too-long command gets only its Not run row; a duplicate gets nothing. Other rows can come between the echo and that row.

command_uuid.description: The queued command's uuid — the client-supplied uuid on the inbound message. Commands enqueued without a uuid (e.g. the one-shot `-p "prompt"` string path) emit no lifecycle events. Renamed from Engine 'uuid' to avoid collision with the universal message uuid field.

wakeup_source.description: Only on 'started', and only when the command being started is a scheduler fire. `loop_wakeup`: a ScheduleWakeup (dynamic /loop) wakeup has fired; `scheduled_for` gives the time it was set for. `schedule_wakeup`: any other scheduled-task fire, such as a CronCreate job or the notice for scheduled tasks that were missed. The values match the UserPromptSubmit hook's `source`. A fire removed from the queue without being started (for example by an interrupt with cancel_queued, or by end_session) gets only its terminal state, without this key. Advertised by the `lifecycle_wakeup_source_v1` capability on system/init.

scheduled_for.description: Only beside `loop_wakeup`: the time, in epoch milliseconds, that the fired wakeup was set for; when a ScheduleWakeup call armed it, this equals the `scheduledFor` in that call's result. The fire itself can come earlier or later than that time. A host that keeps an idle session alive for a wakeup should stop waiting only when this equals the time it is waiting for: while this fire sat in the queue, a turn may have armed a newer wakeup, which is still pending. A fire that never starts (its prompt could not be prepared, the input had closed, or it was removed from the queue) sends no such frame, so the host also needs a time limit of its own past this time.

ran_ahead.description: @internal Only on a repeated 'queued' frame, written only to the VS Code panel: the plugin hooks of this `immediate` command, typed during a turn, have run and answered ahead of its turn. The command is still queued, and its own turn prints the answer.

command_lifecycleOutput.description: @internal Fate of a queued command (slash command or queued user prompt). 'queued' when the inbound message enters the command queue; 'started' when it drains into a turn; then exactly one terminal state: 'completed' — the turn that consumed it ended cleanly; 'cancelled' — removed by cancel_async_message (the host's own, or — with Remote Control enabled (remote_control) — a remote client withdrawing a prompt that a remote client queued: such a uuid was never sent by the host, so there is nothing to resend and the frame is informational), swept by an interrupt with cancel_queued:true, caught by a pending cancel just before dispatch, or consumed into a turn that was aborted (interrupt) or died on a hard failure (model_error, prompt_too_long, ...) — cancelled-over-completed is deliberate dup-over-loss for exactly-once resenders, so a fold answered earlier in a failed turn may be re-sent (a per-fold ledger refinement is tracked separately) — but resenders must not blindly resend on 'cancelled': user-requested removals arrive as the same state, so correlate against your own cancel_async_message responses AND against any interrupt receipt's `cancelled` list (interrupt_cancel_queued_v1) and resend only cancels neither source accounts for; 'discarded' — the session ended (end_session) with the command still queued, or with a peer message still held by the receive-side policy (not preceded by 'queued' then); 'refused' — declined by the session's receive-side policy before entering the queue (outright, or after being held): not preceded by 'queued', and it will not run in this session. Known gap: folds consumed by turns ending via max_turns / hook_stopped / tool_deferred / background_requested report 'completed' even though their content may only be answered on continuation/resume. A prompt sent with requeue_if_interrupted_within_ms that an interrupt puts back reports 'queued' again (after its 'started', if that was reported), then goes on as any queued prompt does. 'completed' means the consuming turn ended, not that the result frame was delivered. Ordering relative to the result frame is per-path: a command that starts a fresh turn emits 'completed' AFTER that turn's result frame (later still when the result is held back for background tasks); a command folded into an already-in-flight turn emits 'completed' BEFORE that turn's result frame. Not a strict pairing: a terminal state may arrive for a command_uuid that never emitted 'started' (control-request ACKs, duplicate deliveries); internally-enqueued commands (cron triggers, teammate shutdown prompts, deferred-turn resume) mint a fresh uuid at enqueue and emit started/terminal without 'queued'; a turn that fails by throwing can leave 'started' without a terminal state; and a peer message the queue's own admission guard drops after acceptance (rate limit, duplicate collapse, loop guard, queued-peer cap) currently leaves 'queued' without a terminal state — on process exit a wrapper should synthesize 'discarded' for uuids it has not seen reach a terminal state. trigger.description: What discarded the conversation: 'clear' is the /clear command (or its /reset and /new aliases), 'plan_mode_exit' is leaving plan mode with the clear-context option, 'fresh_session' is a flow that starts a fresh session to implement an approved plan, 'onboarding' is an onboarding flow re-run inside an existing session. user_message_uuid.description: Only with trigger 'clear': the uuid of the user message whose /clear was executed (the client's own uuid for that message when it came from a Remote Control or stream-json client, otherwise the uuid the CLI assigned to the typed command). timestamp.description: When the reset happened, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC read from the clock of the process that performed it. out___schema158.description: @internal Typed kind of the API error when is_api_error_message is true, for consumers that key on the cause instead of the message text (the text stays the fallback and may change). Absent when the error has no typed kind; new values are added over time, so treat an unknown value as absent. dlp_request_denied: the request was refused by the organization's data-loss-prevention policy — terminal for that request body; a consumer replaying history must not re-send it. claude_code_version_too_old: the API refused the request because this Claude Code build is below a required minimum version — the selected model's minimum, or an organization-policy floor; only the message text says which and names the versions, and the remedy is updating Claude Code. safety_monitor_blocked: a server-side safety monitor blocked the model's response for this turn; terminal for the turn, so a consumer replaying history must not re-send the prompt that led to it. effort_requires_thinking: the model refuses the requested effort level while thinking is off; api_error_params.effort names the level. advisor_incompatible: the configured advisor model cannot be paired with this request's model. tool_history_mismatch: the API rejected the conversation's tool_use/tool_result pairing (a tool_use without its result, an orphaned tool_result, a duplicate tool_use id); re-sending the same history fails the same way, and rewinding the conversation is the remedy. autocompact_thrashing: the context refilled to the limit right after each automatic compaction, repeatedly, so the turn stopped; something in context is too large for the window. pdf_too_large: a PDF is over the API's page or size limit. pdf_password_protected: a PDF is encrypted. media_removed: the API refused an image or a document in the conversation, so Claude Code leaves it out of the requests that follow. The frame comes either before the answer of a retry that already left it out, or as the error that ended the turn (the result then repeats this value). api_error_params.media_reason says why, and api_error_params.media which kind of block. Other kinds (pdf_too_large, pdf_password_protected) and some untyped errors also leave the block out, so the absence of this value does not mean that nothing was left out. no_response: no response arrived before the first-byte deadline on any attempt, usually a proxy or gateway that holds responses until they complete. tls_untrusted_ca: the API's TLS certificate comes from an authority this process does not trust, usually a TLS-inspecting proxy or a gateway signed by a private CA. gateway_content_type: a proxy between Claude Code and Amazon Bedrock rewrote Bedrock's event-stream response. provider_credentials: a third-party cloud provider (api_error_params.provider) refused the request's credentials or access; api_error_params.remedy says what fixes it. gateway_signin_required: the Cloud gateway provider is configured and nobody is signed in to it; no request was sent. gateway_session_expired: the Cloud gateway session expired; no request was sent; api_error_params.remedy is gateway_token when the token came from the environment, which signing in does not replace. api_key_auth_disabled: the organization turned off API key authentication and the active credential is an API key. org_disabled_credential: the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable belongs to a disabled organization and overrides the account sign-in. invalid_credential_header: a credential or header value (from the environment, a helper, or the saved sign-in) cannot be sent as an HTTP header; caught before the request was sent. model_requires_usage_credits: the model runs on usage credits for this account, and credits are off or the included allowance is used up. long_context_credits_required: a request over the 200K-token context boundary needs usage credits. consent_unanswered: the model now uses usage credits and the prompt to confirm went unanswered; nothing was sent. no_allowed_fallback: switching off the model was needed (the usage-credits prompt was declined) and the model policy allows no other model. model_substitution_disabled: switching off the model was needed and CLAUDE_CODE_NO_MODEL_FALLBACK forbids it. field_not_granted: the organization is not allowed to send a field in the request, and the message text says what to do. usage_limit_reached: the request was refused by the account's own usage limit, a plan limit (session, weekly or per-model) or a spend cap on usage credits; api_error_params.rate_limit_info says which and when it resets. The other refusals that share error rate_limit never carry it: an organization policy that turned the service off (no limit was reached, and no reset clears it), a temporary server throttle, a capacity switch-off, an entitlement refusal shown in the server's own words, or a 429 on an API key or a third-party cloud provider. empty_completion: the model ended its turn with no visible text, and its one retry had no content block, on a person's own prompt with no reply and no tool result after it; the turn ends as an error so that a host shows a failure and not a blank reply. unattended_start_limit: a cloud session's process that starts where an earlier one died carries on what that one left unfinished; by the session's record, as many processes as are allowed (a number that is configured; with none there is no limit) had already done so within 24 hours with no message from a person in between, and this one did not; no request was sent; terminal for the turn, so a consumer replaying history must not re-send the prompt that led to it; anything new sent to the session runs as usual; a person's message allows it again, and so does time, as earlier starts pass out of the 24 hours. unattended_start_unconfirmed: a cloud session's process did not carry on what an earlier one left unfinished, because it could not check whether it was allowed to: the session's record of such starts could not be read or written, or the check failed; no request was sent; not terminal: a later process may carry the turn on.

unifiedWindows.description: @internal Per-window usage for the session (5-hour), weekly (7-day), and overage-included weekly (per-model bucket; present only for accounts whose responses carry that window) subscription rate-limit windows, as read from the anthropic-ratelimit-unified-* response headers. utilization is the fraction of the window used (usually 0-1, same scale as the top-level utilization field; values above 1 occur when usage legitimately runs past a window's cap, e.g. lower-priority episodes past the 5-hour limit); resetsAt is unix epoch seconds. status is the status the server sent for the window: allowed_warning once past a warning threshold, rejected at or past its limit. A rejected window alone does not mean requests are refused; the top-level status says whether they are. surpassedThreshold is the highest warning threshold passed, as a fraction of the limit (1 once rejected). Each is absent when the server sent none or a value this version cannot read. Unlike the top-level status/utilization fields, which describe the currently limiting window, every window is tracked on every observation, and events are emitted when a window's rounded percentage, reset time, status or threshold moves, not only on status transitions. Windows absent from the account state are absent here. Absent until the first response carrying these headers is observed, and always absent for API-key, Bedrock, and Vertex sessions, whose responses do not carry them.

rateLimitGraceActive.description: @internal Usage-limit grace signal. Follows the latest served main-loop or subagent response: set when it reports grace-zone utilization > 0 (the server reports that only to a request that sent `anthropic-usage-limit: extended`, tengu_lantern_spool), cleared when a response the limiter ran on reports none or, if the latest in-zone response named the grace window's reset, once that reset passes on this machine's clock. Side calls, and responses with no `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status` (the limiter did not run), are not read. A refused request's 429 is not read either, so while requests are refused the last value persists: still expire any UI derived from this field via resetsAt. While set, overageStatus allowed / allowed_warning means paid extra usage covers the overflow (nothing will be cut off). Stays true at hard exhaustion (status rejected); combine with status instead of reading this field alone as "still usable".

overagePeriodMonthly.description: @internal Monthly service spend-cap telemetry for the Claude-in-Slack surface (CLAUDE_IN_SLACK_V2): utilization is fraction-of-cap.

overagePeriodChannel.description: @internal Per-Slack-channel spend-cap telemetry for the Claude-in-Slack surface (CLAUDE_IN_SLACK_V2): utilization is fraction-of-cap. Absent when the channel has no individual cap.

limitScope.description: Which spend limit blocked the request when it is not the member's own cap: 'group_pool' means a pooled group budget shared by the member's team is used up (the denial otherwise looks like the member's own monthly cap). Absent on a plain member denial and from older CLIs.

usageCreditOffer.description: @internal A limited-time offer on usage credits the account holds at this limit, for the IDE extension's limit banner: the kind (a steeper discount, or extra credit for the same price), the headline percent every credit pack meets or beats, whole days left in the account's offer window, and the ready-made banner text. Present only on a rejected frame from a session the VS Code extension owns, once the server has answered that the account holds an active offer; absent otherwise. The prices themselves apply wherever the credits are bought.

adminRequestOffer.description: @internal The IDE limit banner's offer to ask the member's admin for a higher spend limit: its state (can ask, already pending, sending, sent), its copy, whether the last filing failed, and a counter that moves when a click could not be acted on. Present only on a rejected frame from a VS Code extension session for a Team or Enterprise member at their own spend limit, while tengu_tallow_quoit serves it, its kill switch is on and the organization's requests are not switched off.

out___schema162.description: Rate limit information for claude.ai subscription users.

out___schema264.description: Structured tool output — the tool's full Output object, not the string content sent to the model. The shape is per-tool, keyed by the matching tool_use block's name (see the *Output types in toolTypes); MCP and dynamic tools carry their own shapes, so the field stays unknown-typed. For the Agent/Task tool the completed shape is the subagent's final report without the model-directed agentId/usage trailer, plus run totals — render from it instead of parsing the tool_result text. A call that stepped aside for a message the user sent (today a WebFetch or WebSearch call) carries `{ detachedToolCall: true }` in place of its Output: the call is still running, and its result reaches the model in a later turn.

out___schema267.description: @internal Input only. Asks the CLI to put this prompt back in its queue, instead of losing it, when an interrupt crosses with a running turn taking the prompt in: the interrupt was sent while its sender still believed the prompt was waiting. The value says for how long an interrupt is taken to have been sent so: a whole number of milliseconds from 1, and above 10000 it counts as 10000. The time runs from the moment the turn announces the model request that carries the prompt (system/status 'requesting', which is on the wire only with partial messages); until then it has not begun. The prompt is put back when an interrupt control request without cancel_queued stops that turn within the time and before the model's next reply has begun to arrive. It goes back to the front of the queue under the same uuid and runs in a later turn of its own, after any queued prompt of higher priority; prompts queued behind it are not merged into that turn's prompt, though the turn can take them in as any turn does. The interrupt's response lists it under still_queued and under put_back, and from then on cancel_async_message can withdraw it. The stopped turn reports no 'cancelled' for it, counts it in its result's queued_turn_count (if its origin is stamped user-driven, as for any queued prompt) and leaves it out of that result's user_message_uuids (on an error result an empty list, with no user_message_uuid, if nothing else is listed). On stdout it reports command_lifecycle 'queued' a second time; over a remote transport its delivery is not reported 'processed' until its later turn ends. With cancel_queued:true it stays with the stopped turn and is not listed under the response's cancelled. The row the stopped turn wrote for it (a queued_command attachment) leaves the conversation and is never stored, so the model sees the prompt once; until the prompt can no longer be put back, that row and the rows after it are kept out of the stored transcript. UserPromptSubmit hooks run for it twice, and what they added to the stopped turn stays. If a compaction begins while that row is kept out, the row is stored at once and stays in the conversation, so the prompt, if an interrupt puts it back or has just done so, is seen twice. A prompt is put back at most once, and never after the host's own cancel_async_message for it answered cancelled:false. Of several prompts taken in since the model last spoke, only the last can be put back; the others stay with the stopped turn. The field is ignored when it is not such a number, when the message has no uuid or has shouldQuery:false, and when the message is not a person's own typing: a synthetic, hidden, client-composed, seeded, peer or relayed message, one that declares a non-human origin, or one whose client_platform names no app or keyboard that a person types in. claude-code-server also needs a client_platform, and one that names an app. A CLI that does not advertise interrupt_requeue_taken_v1 on system/init ignores the field too.

out___schema320.description: @internal No person typed this message's text in this session (a server or an app composed it). The text is delivered as written and is not treated as typing: no slash-command dispatch, no at-mention expansion beyond the message's own uploaded files, no reminder or command from keywords in it, and a skill named in it does not count as typed by the user. Who sent the message, and whether a person is present, stays with its origin. The checks of whether a message's words are the user's own do not read this mark yet: they too go by the origin. Unlike client_composed, the turn-start attachment pass still runs. Any value other than false or null is read as true.

servers.description: mcp_needs_auth / mcp_disabled: the server names as configured. mcp_required_missing: the name patterns the agent definition requires that no connected server matches.

provider.description: auth_expired / auth_overridden / auth_missing_scope / design_needs_authorization: whose login the fix names — 'claude_ai' (the claude.ai account, /login) or 'claude_design' (Claude Design's own authorization, /design login).

path.description: outside_reads_blocked: the path the read block refused, when the refusal names one. staged_for_review: the settings file the write was held for.

managed.description: outside_reads_blocked: an organization policy sets the block, so the user cannot remove it. auth_overridden: the overriding credential was injected by the host environment, so nothing in this session can unset it.

feature.description: feature_disabled / policy_denied: the feature that is off.

cause.description: feature_disabled: why the feature is off — 'managed_settings' (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS, or disableWorkflows or enableWorkflows: false set by a layer above the user's own settings), 'org_policy', 'unavailable' (not launched for this account), 'user_setting' (the user's /config setting is off, including a disableWorkflows in their own settings, and nothing the user cannot clear also keeps them off), or 'unsupported_runtime' (this Claude Code process is not running on Bun, the runtime its binary is built with, and workflow scripts run only there).

policy_kind.description: policy_denied: the verdict — 'org_denied' (the organization's policy turns the feature off) or 'latched' (a HIPAA-regulated organization signed in earlier in this process; restarting clears it).

remedy.description: @internal The fix a host can offer for a tool result, stamped from structured producer state (never parsed from the result text). Kinds: mcp_needs_auth, mcp_disabled, mcp_required_missing, auth_expired, auth_overridden, auth_missing_scope, design_needs_authorization, sandbox_violation, outside_reads_blocked, memory_paused, feature_disabled, policy_denied, spawn_arg_limit (the command's exec image exceeded the OS argument limit), staged_for_review (a settings-file write held for the machine owner's review). New kinds are additive; treat an unknown kind as absent.

out___schema336.description: @internal Display metadata for this message's tool_result blocks, keyed by tool_use_id. non_execution_kind is the harness-stamped reason an is_error:true result did not carry the tool's own execution output (user-rejected / permission-rule / automode-* / interrupted / cancelled); absent means the tool ran to completion. remedy is the fix a host can offer for what the result reports (see SDKToolResultRemedy). An entry may carry a remedy alone, on a result that did run (a staged write, a sandbox violation on exit 0), so whether a call ran is read from non_execution_kind, never from an entry's presence. On a subagent's messages (parent_tool_use_id set), entries carry only permission_decision, so those messages do not say whether a call ran. permission_decision is how the call's permission check ended, as Claude Code's claude_code.tool.blocked_on_user trace span reports it. decision is accept, reject or cancelled. source names what decided: config, classifier, hook, user_temporary, user_permanent, user_reject, user_abort, or invalid_input, permission_updated_input_invalid or server_fallback_tombstone when bad input or the server ended the wait. Which label a rule gets depends on the session: in SDK sessions a rule for this session or in the user's own settings reports user_temporary, user_permanent or user_reject and other rules report config, while interactive sessions report every rule as config. reason_type is the kind of reason the check gave when it decided by itself, such as 'rule' whenever a rule decided, or 'classifier' for an auto-mode allow, which reports source config. reason_type is absent when a person or the SDK host answered the question, when the check's outcome was still a question, and for user_abort and the last three sources above. permission_decision is absent when the call ended before its permission check, and on some results built apart from the call's own run, such as a plugin hook's refusal, a hook's rewrite of a denied result, or the result the tool executor writes for a queued call that a stop cancelled. user_feedback is the deny comment a human typed at a permission prompt (the local dialog or a bridge client's deny UI), before the CLI's reject-message framing — absent when the deny was resolved by a coordinator, channel relay, or hook rather than a human. A deny answered through the SDK control protocol (can_use_tool / --permission-prompt-tool) currently reports as 'permission-rule' with no user_feedback, because that wire carries no human-provenance signal. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content` — so it is not replayed to the model. Clients read this instead of string-matching the result prose.

iterations.description: Per-iteration usage when the request ran several sampling iterations.

fallback_credit.description: Outcome of a fallback-credit token the request presented, or null.

spawned.description: Subagents actually started (one tengu_agent_tool_selected each); a refused or failed launch is not counted.

requested.description: Spawns by the run_in_background value the model passed; all count as unset while the parameter is not offered (background tasks disabled, or subagents forced into the background: in a terminal, the desktop app or the VS Code extension, or with CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=1).

started_in_background.description: Spawns that started in the background after defaults and session settings (tengu_agent_tool_selected.is_async); the rest blocked the spawning tool call.

max_depth.description: Deepest spawn: 1 = started by the main thread, 2 = by a depth-1 subagent.

spawned_by_subagents.description: Spawns made from inside another subagent (depth > 1).

killed.description: Stopped before finishing: parent = by another agent through TaskStop; system = by Claude Code itself (the --max-budget-usd halt, the sweep of background subagents when an SDK or IDE client interrupts, or -p giving up on a background subagent still running at its wait ceiling); user = any other stop, including a foreground subagent cancelled just as it finished (counted here, not as completed).

refused.description: Agent tool calls turned down because one of these limits was reached (other denials, such as an unknown agent type, are not counted). depth_limit stays near zero in practice: a subagent at the nesting limit is normally not offered the tool at all.

out___schema426.description: @internal Subagents started through the Agent tool in this session, as running totals (forked skills, workflows, teammates and other internal agents are not counted; two sessions in one process keep separate counts). Cumulative like modelUsage: read the latest result rather than summing across results; a resumed session starts fresh and a mid-session /clear zeroes it, though a background subagent that outlives the /clear still records its outcome, so completed, failed and killed can then exceed spawned. A result that was held back while background subagents finished carries the counts as of when it is written to the stream, as do its total_cost_usd, duration_api_ms and modelUsage (and usage where that is a running total; a per-turn main-loop usage keeps its turn-end value). Omitted by hosts without a local Agent tool and on crash/startup-error results; all zeros until the Agent tool starts or refuses a subagent. A remote (isolation: remote) launch counts as spawned but never reports an outcome. Per-subagent detail is on the task_started / task_notification events.

prompt_suggestionOutput.description: Predicted next user prompt, emitted after each turn when promptSuggestions is enabled.

notification_id.description: Server-assigned stable id — the dedup key across redeliveries.

origin.description: Server-attested source token: "github_webhook" | "trigger_fire" | "mcp_send_message" (open set; unknown values render verbatim).

content.description: Exactly the text that would previously have been injected as a user turn, framing included.

queued_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp of when the backend queued it.

queued_notificationInput.description: @internal Backend→CLI: a trigger delivery (webhook activity, scheduled trigger, agent message) queued server-side instead of injected as a user turn. The CLI buffers it, nudges the model to call the ReadNotifications tool, and acks the event processed only when drained — an undrained event redelivers on resume.

rate_limit_eventOutput.description: Rate limit event emitted when rate limit info changes.

total_cost_usd.description: Cumulative estimated cost in USD for this query() call, covering the same query-pipeline calls as modelUsage and sharing its lifecycle: cumulative across turns in streaming-input sessions — each result carries the running total so far, so read the latest result rather than summing across results. Crash/startup-error results may carry zeroed values, a resumed or forked session continues from the total its transcript saved, when it has one (so the first result already carries the earlier turns; maxBudgetUsd counts only the spend since this query() call started or last /clear), and a mid-session /clear resets the running total. An estimate, not a billing statement.

usage.description: MAIN AGENT LOOP ONLY — excludes Task subagent, sidechain, and auxiliary model calls, and is per-turn in streaming-input sessions. Prefer modelUsage for token/cost accounting.

modelUsage.description: Per-model totals for every model call made through the query pipeline during this query() call — main loop, Task subagents, sidechains, and internal calls such as compaction and Workflow agents. Cumulative across turns in streaming-input sessions: each result carries the running total so far, so read the latest result rather than summing across results. Internal helper calls outside the query pipeline (e.g. the permission classifier, token-count probes) are excluded; crash/startup-error results may carry zeroed usage, a resumed or forked session continues from the totals its transcript saved, when it has them (so the first result already carries the earlier turns), and a mid-session /clear resets the running total. The correct field for token/cost accounting; treat it as an estimate, not a billing statement.

model_usage_since_last_result.description: @internal Per-model usage and cost of the calls this process counted since it wrote its previous result (since it started, for its first), keyed and shaped like modelUsage and covering the same calls. Sum it over a conversation's results instead of subtracting modelUsage totals: within a conversation each call is stated on at most one result, whatever a resume or a kill does to modelUsage. Calls that finish after a result (a background subagent, a late title call) are stated on the next result, and a /clear's own result states what was counted before it. Nothing is carried from one process to the next, so what a process counted after its last result is stated nowhere. That includes the finished calls of a turn in flight when the process is shut down or killed, even where another process carries the turn on and writes its result. A result whose write fails loses its usage too (result_index shows the gap). A Workflow agent that runs as a cloud session of its own is counted here, as in modelUsage, and that session's own results state it too. costBasis, canonicalModel and provider are the latest request's. A model with nothing counted is left out; {} means nothing was counted. Set by a stream-json or --sdk-url run on the results it numbers as it writes them; a result relayed from another process keeps what that process set. Not set on error results numbered by hand (a start-up failure, an error that escapes the run), by --output-format json and text runs, or by older versions. Absent is not {}.

subagent_stats.description: @internal Running totals of the subagents the Agent tool started this session; see SDKSubagentStats.

safety_stops.description: @internal How many times a safety system has stopped one of this session's model calls made through the query pipeline (main loop, subagents, forked skills, compaction and other internal calls), as a running total since the session started in this process; two sessions in one process keep separate counts. Counted: a response that ends on stop_reason refusal, whether Claude Code then shows it, retries it or re-sends it to another model; a refusal that the API itself answered on a fallback model; output that the API's content filter stopped for good (the stop ends the call); and, where the build can recognise it (public builds cannot), a server-side safety monitor's block (api_error safety_monitor_blocked). It counts these events, not calls: one call can add a refusal answered on a fallback model and then that model's own refusal. 0 means that none of these was seen; a kind of stop that this version does not know is not counted. Never sum across results. It is never saved, so a resumed session starts at 0 again, and a mid-session /clear zeroes it: over a stored log that spans a restart, a resume or a /clear, any result above 0 means a stop happened, and a later 0 does not cancel it. Present, 0 included, on every result that carries a turn's measured totals. Absent on the zeroed results that stand in for a crashed, cut or never-started turn, on Remote Control's results and from older producers, where it says nothing: absent is not 0. A call still running when a result is written (a background subagent's) shows on the next result; a result held back while background subagents finished carries the count as of when it is written to the stream, never less than it was built with. Not counted inside the pipeline: a stop of the API's content filter that Claude Code answers by streaming the request again (so 0 does not rule one out), an organization's data-loss-prevention denial (api_error dlp_request_denied), a block by a cloud provider's own guardrail, an advisor's refusal inside a reply that ends normally. Not counted at all: model calls outside the query pipeline (e.g. the permission classifier, token-count probes) and work in other processes.

queued_turn_count.description: User-initiated sends still waiting in the command queue when this result was produced. Greater than 0 means at least one more user turn (and result) follows without further input, barring cancellation; 0 means none is pending, or the session is ending (end_session or a shutdown latched mid-turn discards the backlog). Queued sends may coalesce into fewer turns, so this counts pending sends, not remaining results. System-generated queue entries are not counted. Absent on fatal startup results and on surfaces without a command queue.

phase.description: @internal 'setup' when the session process never started, 'run' when it exited.

runner_exit.description: @internal Set by the self-hosted runner on the result it synthesizes when the session process fails to start or exits abnormally (src/self-hosted-runner/failureResult.ts buildFailureEvents).

startup_failure_reason.description: Set on the zeroed error_during_execution result a stream-json run writes before exiting on a known startup failure; errors carries the same text as stderr. Failures that used to end with stderr alone write that result only when the host sets CLAUDE_CODE_STARTUP_FAILURE_RESULTS. Absent on every other result, on startup failures without a known cause, and from older producers.

user_message_uuid.description: Client uuid of the user message that triggered this turn (submitMessage options.uuid), echoed back so a consumer can link this error result to the send it answers — the same join key the success variant echoes, carried alone (error turns have no request_sent_wall_ms to report). A delivery-failure result from the remote-session client echoes the failed send's queue key, which is client-minted when the host sent no uuid of its own. A synthetic/scheduled (meta) turn's own uuid is echoed only when the host vouches it is the client event's own (delivered content such as a Slack owner ping or a Slack-bot observation); a meta turn that folded queued user messages in mid-turn, vouched or not, echoes the LAST of them. Absent on turns that neither had a client uuid nor folded a user message in, on session-scoped failures with no single triggering send (a crashed worker's zeroed result), and from older producers.

user_message_uuids.description: Client uuids of every user message whose prompt this turn consumed, in consumption order — all members of a prompt batch the host merged into this one turn (several messages sent close together run as one turn whose user_message_uuid is the LAST member's), then any queued user message folded into the running turn between tool rounds, once taken off the queue — so a consumer that sent any of them can bind this result to its own send by finding its uuid anywhere in the list. Always contains user_message_uuid; at most 64 entries; can be longer than the list on the turn's first reply frame. Present when a headless turn that ran echoes user_message_uuid; absent on delivery-failure and zeroed results and from older producers (fall back to user_message_uuid).

resume_reason.description: Why this turn continued one that a worker restart interrupted. Such a turn is the automatic re-run of the interrupted turn (CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN), or one that goes on from the answer to the permission prompt the new worker took over, or from that turn's tool calls still in flight. The value is the host's CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_REASON when it set one (host_draining, checkpoint_restore, container_recreated, …), else 'interrupted_turn'. Present on such a headless turn's result, success or error, with or without an echo (a turn whose opening user prompt could not be vouched for still carries the reason); absent on every other turn (also one that goes on from the answer to any other permission prompt), on the Remote Control bridge's per-turn synthetic results, and from older producers.

process_start_tuning.description: @internal As process_start_tuning on the success result.

process_start_purge_delay_ms.description: @internal As process_start_purge_delay_ms on the success result.

process_garbage_collections.description: @internal As process_garbage_collections on the success result.

terminal_reason.description: Why the query loop terminated. Unset when the loop was bypassed (local slash command).

interrupted_by_shutdown.description: @internal The host of a multi-tenant worker shut the worker down while this turn ran. The shutdown was the first thing to abort the turn, and the turn is left for the session's next worker. The other frames of the ending, and terminal_reason, are the same as for a Stop from a client. Read this member to tell the two apart. A success result can have it, when the shutdown falls in a Stop hook. A result without it can also be the result of a shutdown. A shutdown that makes the turn write no interrupt marker does not set it, and older producers never set it.

result_index.description: Delivery sequence of this result within the run: how many results the run numbered before this one, starting at 0, in the order the process writes them. A result held back while background work finishes is numbered when it is finally written, not when its text was produced; a result whose write fails still consumes its number, so a gap in a stream-json sequence means a result was lost. Distinct from num_turns, which counts model round-trips within one turn. Numbered by the process that hosts the run (`claude -p`, stream-json): a local client relaying a cloud session passes the cloud session's numbering through and its own locally built error results carry none; the in-process engine surface does not number yet. Absent from older producers.

fast_mode_state.description: Fast mode state: off, in cooldown after rate limit, or actively enabled.

fast_mode_disabled_reason.description: Why fast mode can't serve right now. Absent when nothing blocks it (a request may still choose standard speed). A paused-after-rate-limit run is not here; it rides fast_mode_state as 'cooldown'.

fromMode.description: The SENDING session's permission class as declared by the host that injects this message on local stdin ('bypass' for sessions that run tools without asking, 'prompting' otherwise). Lets the recipient deliver a same-class message immediately while a cross-class or undeclared sender is still held at a recipient that runs without asking. Honored only from the injecting host on local stdin; absent when the host does not declare it.

name.description: Sender display name, normalized by the harness: Unicode control, format, surrogate, and line/paragraph-separator code points stripped (categories Cc/Cf/Cs/Zl/Zp — covers bidi controls, zero-width characters, and tag characters), trimmed, at most 64 code points (+ ellipsis, never splitting a surrogate pair). Sender-asserted display text (the addressable identity is `from`) — render it as reported speech, but no client-side character sanitization is needed. Absent when the wire is not exactly one harness-formed envelope and on messages from older senders.

fromSession.description: The sender's host-openable session id (the envelope's `from-session` attribute — e.g. a desktop `local_<uuid>` or a cloud session `session_`/`ses_` id), set by the sender's host so a receiving UI can link this message back to the sending session. Sender-asserted like `from`: a navigation target only, never authority. Absent when the sender's host provides none and on messages from older senders.

inbound_origin.description: @internal Server-asserted ingest path of the demoted delivery, copied at classification from the message-level `inbound_origin`.

senderTaskId.description: Task id of the in-process background subagent that sent this message, stamped by the harness from the sending loop (never from tool input). Absent for cross-session peers.

body.description: Decoded message body with the peer envelope stripped — byte-exact with what the model sees. Present only when the turn is exactly one harness-formed envelope (or an in-process agent message); render this instead of re-parsing the message text.

verifiedPeerPid.description: Kernel-verified pid of the process that connected to this session's cross-session messaging socket, read from the connection (SO_PEERCRED / LOCAL_PEERPID) — never from the payload. This identifies the CONNECTING process, which for relayed traffic (e.g. a daemon forwarding on another session's behalf) is the relay, not the message's author. Key sender identity on this, never on `from`: `from` is sender-authored and kept only for reply routing, so it is forgeable by any same-user process. Absent when unverifiable (Windows, non-UDS ingress) — never a wrong value. Pids are recyclable: provenance, not an authentication token.

handback.description: @internal Present, and always true, when the message is a subagent's final report to the agent that launched it, delivered through the SubagentHandback tool. Stamped by the harness, never from tool input. `body` is then the hand-back frame line with the indented report under it, and any harness note above it; `handbackReportText` and `handbackNote` carry those two parts for display. A boolean mark: not the `handback` state string of a task notification or of an Agent tool result. A hand-back is never joined, so neither this mark nor `flagged` appears beside `members`.

flagged.description: @internal Present, and always true, on a hand-back that auto mode's review blocked, or that it could not judge because a safety filter refused the review request: the report was delivered all the same, under the SECURITY WARNING that `handbackNote` carries. Never cap or fold such a message: show the note and the report in full. Absent on a hand-back that was not flagged, including one delivered under the note that the review was unavailable.

handbackNote.description: @internal On a hand-back: the note the harness composed above the frame line in `body`, without the indent. On a blocked report it quotes the review's reason, which can quote the report, so show it as untrusted text. Absent when there is no note.

handbackReportText.description: @internal On a hand-back: the subagent's report as the model reads it, under the frame line in `body`, without the indent. Draw it as a separate element from `handbackNote`: the two fields are their only boundary. Absent wherever `body` is and on a message that is not a hand-back.

members.description: @internal On a prompt that joins several queued messages from this sender: the joined messages in the order the model reads them, each with its own `body`. The origin's `body` is then absent. Absent on a message that was not joined and when any joined message had no `body`.

subkind.description: Present when the delivery is the fired stored prompt of a scheduled task/routine ('scheduled-trigger', stamped from server-asserted provenance, or declared by a local host for its own scheduled runs; the schedule attests storage, not authorship) or a coordinator co-member SendMessage delivery ('peer-send-message': model-authored text from another of the same user's sessions, verified by the server-stamped receiver co-membership — task-notification for prompt authority, but distinguishable so the receive-side crossSessionInbound setting can apply to it). The harness frames a scheduled-trigger delivery as the session's assigned task instead of the generic background-notification frame. Absent on webhook, PR-steward, plugin, and background-event deliveries.

fireReason.description: On a 'scheduled-trigger' delivery, why it fired: a short lowercase token such as 'scheduled', 'manual', 'retry', 'catch_up' or 'api'. Set by the server for cloud routines, or declared by a local host for its own scheduled runs, which is honored only in a process the host started with CLAUDE_CODE_HOST_SCHEDULED_RUN=1 (a local host's value is kept only if it is 1 to 32 lowercase letters or underscores); absent when neither sent one.

producer.description: @internal Present ('session-task') when the notification reports on work this session itself launched: a background agent, shell command, workflow, monitor, MCP or remote task settling, a detached tool call, or a hook rewake or worker check-in following up on such work. Absent on webhook, artifact and other externally-authored deliveries.

runId.description: On a background task's own notification: the run_id its task_* events carried, as of when the notification was queued. Not part of the text the model reads.

taskKind.description: @internal Present ('mcp-task') only on a notification that an MCP server's own task has ended, and not on every one. Narrower than task_type 'mcp_task', which also covers an MCP tool call moved to the background.

oneOf.description: Injected turn whose ingress classification found no provenance. Framed by the harness as a non-user source in both drains; never presumed human, never host-replayed.
Report from a background observer agent to the agent it observes. One-way by construction — the observed agent must not reply.
Activity digest delivered to an observer agent. The message body is the self-framing digest (envelope + postamble); observed content is data, not instructions.

origin.description: Provenance of a user-role message (peer session, team lead, channel). A host wrapping keyboard input must stamp {kind:'human'} explicitly — absent origin is treated as unattributed and fails closed at strict isHuman() trust gates.

time_to_request_phases_ms.description: @internal How time_to_request_ms was spent, in integer ms per phase, summing to it exactly: system_prompt, resume_other (settling, before the turn's own prompt, tool calls that an earlier run left open or the session's client handed over, see turn_start_resume_kind; excluding four parts of it that have keys of their own: resume_store_confirm, writing a handed-over turn's lines to the transcript and waiting for the store to confirm them; resume_staged_files_wait, that turn's wait for files its client is still staging; resume_connector_wait, an orphaned permission's wait for its tool's MCP server to connect; turn_start_tool_run, the calls' permission checks, a person's time at a prompt included, and their runs, which are work the user asked for, not preparation; older producers report these five as one key, turn_start_resume), process_user_input (excluding four parts of it that have keys of their own: input_images, input_attachments, input_command, input_hooks), transcript_persist, tool_pool_refresh, system_prompt_rebuild (a second assembly of the system prompt, run when the tool pool re-read after the message was handled differs from the turn-start pool; older producers report it inside system_prompt), init_message, engine_pickup, memory_recall_wait, memory_context_wait, message_prep, model_config_wait, autocompact, query_setup, auto_mode_context_wait (the wait at dispatch for the auto-mode context, on a request that started one), model_gates, tool_schema_build, message_normalization, client_creation, request_build, then at most one of redrive_reactive_compact, redrive_fallback_model, redrive_non_streaming and redrive_other (present when the first model request of the turn never began streaming, or was answered without streaming, so time_to_request_ms runs to the send time of a later request: the time between the two sends, named for the reason; after a reply without streaming it includes that reply and any tool calls), and other (the remainder no phase covers). A phase that did not run on the turn is absent; other is always present. Present where time_to_request_ms is, on CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE sessions and hosts that set CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_STARTUP_TIMING; absent elsewhere and from older producers.

turn_start_resume_kind.description: @internal What the turn was given to settle before its own prompt (the resume_ phases and turn_start_tool_run in time_to_request_phases_ms say how long that took): orphaned_permission (a permission answer whose pending request was lost, as when a worker restarts, so the tool call is settled with that answer), turn_handoff (a turn in progress that the session's client handed over), deferred_tool_use (a call a PreToolUse hook deferred), or none (resume_other is still reported, at about 0). A turn given more than one reports the first in that order. Present where time_to_request_phases_ms is.
