On connections that persist frames server-side (the local bridge-worker lane) this key is always omitted — the skipped-entry detail stays in the local log, so an omitted key there does NOT assert every entry validated.

fast_mode_state.description: Fast mode state: off, in cooldown after rate limit, or actively enabled.

fast_mode_disabled_reason.description: Why fast mode can't serve right now. Absent when nothing blocks it (a request may still choose standard speed). A paused-after-rate-limit run is not here; it rides fast_mode_state as 'cooldown'.

text.description: The label to show — already sanitized to a single line of plain text and capped at 6 columns, exactly as the terminal footer renders it after its ◆ glyph.

footer_indicator.description: @internal The terminal's configured "◆ <text>" footer pill — see SDKFooterIndicator. Absent when nothing is configured.

effort.description: The effort level the session will send on its next request — after env overrides, session state, org caps and model-support downgrades; the same value get_settings reports as applied.effort. null when no effort parameter will be sent (a model without effort, CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=unset, or an internal numeric budget). Present on Remote Control bridge init frames (terminal- and Desktop/VS Code-hosted sessions); absent on hosts that do not publish it and on CLIs that predate the field. Re-emitted inits carry the current value — the newest frame wins.

per_turn_effort_active.description: @internal Whether per-turn effort is active for this frame's `model`. true: an effort change keeps the prompt cache, because the effort is sent inside the conversation, at the turn where it changes. false: the effort is sent only as the top-level parameter, so a change rewrites the cached prefix. Mid-session the CLI reports only a change to false (system/per_turn_effort_changed), and true comes only from an init. After a fresh process, or after the conversation's refusals are cleared (for example by /clear or a compaction), a true is provisional: a refusal on any later request sends system/per_turn_effort_changed before the retry, so a host keeps listening for it all session. Absent means unknown. Sent by the stream-json (Agent SDK) host.

view_mode.description: Whether the session's transcript is in focus view ('focus': the model is told the user sees only its final message per turn, so clients may collapse each turn to the prompt and the final response; 'default' otherwise). Toggled by /focus, including over Remote Control. Present on Remote Control bridge init frames and on the per-turn init of headless stream-json runs (`claude rc` workers, -p, the SDK's subprocess transport); absent on hosts that do not publish it (the in-process engine) and on CLIs that predate the field. Re-emitted inits carry the current value — the newest frame wins.

capabilities.description: Protocol capabilities this CLI supports, so SDK consumers can feature-detect instead of version-sniffing. Open set — ignore unknown values; check each capability for exactly the behavior you use. 'interrupt_receipt_v1' = the interrupt control_response success payload carries still_queued (uuids of async user messages that survive the interrupt). 'interrupt_cancel_queued_v1' = the interrupt control_request honors cancel_queued:true (queued and pending-dispatch commands are cancelled alongside the abort, listed on the response's cancelled field; still_queued is then empty — including any uuid that was mid-fold at the interrupt instant, since this request also aborts and the fold never delivers it — except that a client driving a hosted session lists there what it can no longer recall: a send already in flight to that session, or the first prompt the session was created with). 'queued_notifications' = the CLI accepts inbound queued_notification stream messages and drains them via ReadNotifications (the cloud session backend reads this from the persisted init event to decide whether it may send them). Absent on older CLIs.

analytics_disabled.description: @internal True when the CLI has analytics/telemetry disabled (privacy level, DO_NOT_TRACK, or 3P provider). IDE clients use this to hide per-message thumbs feedback UI since the rating event would be a no-op.

product_feedback_disabled.description: @internal True when the org's allow_product_feedback policy is false (ZDR/HIPAA). IDE clients use this to hide feedback surfaces (thumbs, session survey) whose events the CLI would drop at the proxy boundary anyway.

memory_paths.description: @internal Absolute directory paths for the auto-memory and team-memory stores. Lets SDK renderers classify Read/Write/Edit tool calls on these paths as memory operations without re-implementing CLI path detection.

scratchpad_path.description: @internal Absolute path of this session's scratchpad directory, for clients that read files from the session. Omitted when the scratchpad is disabled, and from the redacted init sent over the Remote Control bridge and by the hosted worker.

original_cwd.description: @internal Absolute path of the folder the session's file permission checks are anchored at, for clients that read files from the session. Unlike cwd it does not follow the shell: it moves only on /cd, on entering or leaving a worktree, and on a session restore. Omitted on the lanes that redact system/init's local paths: the init sent over the Remote Control bridge and by the claude-code-server tenant worker. Omitted too in a session that has no directory, where cwd is the empty string, and, on every lane, for an organization that is under HIPAA or whose policy the session fetches but does not hold.

additional_directories.description: @internal Absolute paths of the folders added to the session (--add-dir, the SDK additionalDirectories option, settings, a grant or a host's request made mid-session), in no particular order; an empty array when there are none. Re-read for every init message. Left out: a folder that only a settings file the repository delivers adds (.claude/settings.json, and .claude/settings.local.json unless git is known not to track it), so that a branch cannot widen what a client fetches; and an entry not stored as an absolute path. Entries are not all symlink-resolved, and one can be the symlinked spelling of the start folder. It grants nothing: the CLI's own check decides every read. Absent means not told, not none: omitted on the lanes that redact system/init's local paths and for an organization that is under HIPAA or whose policy the session fetches but does not hold, like original_cwd, and by a host that has not wired it. A session that has no directory still sends it.

worker_epoch.description: @internal This cloud worker's life (CLAUDE_CODE_WORKER_EPOCH): a new number each time the session's worker is started. A claude --cloud client that latched an acknowledged epoch (remote_tools_announce) re-registers only when this differs. Emitted on workers where the account's remote-tools gate (tengu_violin_wood) is on, and by every claude-code-server worker whatever that gate reads; absent outside cloud workers and on CLIs that predate the field.

powershell_path.description: @internal Windows only: the absolute path of the PowerShell binary this session runs PowerShell commands with (PowerShell 7 when installed, including Microsoft Store installs, else Windows PowerShell 5.1), or null when none was found. Lets a desktop host open its own terminal with the same shell instead of re-implementing the detection. Present on stream-json (Agent SDK) init frames; absent on other platforms, wherever the init ambient is redacted (the Remote Control bridge), and on CLIs that predate the field.

cloud_session.description: @internal Only on init frames written by the headless stream-json client of a cloud-hosted session (agent loop in the cloud container; this machine may be bound to it as a device): a snapshot per frame, absent in every other mode; no user, assistant or result frame precedes the first such init (informational system frames may; so may a worker's result that no init preceded, after all that was held ahead of it; on a re-attach so may frames of a turn already in progress, other clients' prompts, and the echo of this host's own prompt when the session already had it or it joins a turn in progress). `id` is the cloud session id, always in its `session_…` spelling (the producer normalizes the service's `cse_…` spelling of the same session); hosts store it and pass it back verbatim to re-attach. The frame-level `session_id` is instead the cloud worker's id, a uuidv5 of the session id in its `cse_` form: the same for the life of the cloud session across worker restarts and re-attaches until a /clear in the session, and passed through by the client unchanged. When `device.status` is `unbound`, `reason` is one of the client's unbound-reason keys and `message` its phrase: one line, at most 200 characters, no ANSI or trailing newline, worded to follow `Laptop tools unavailable: `. `directory_sync`: see docs/cloud-session-block.md. `not_applied`, when present, lists what the host passed that this session does not apply — `name` is a flag as `--flag`, a key inside --settings / --managed-settings as `settings.<key>` / `managed-settings.<key>`, or a field of the opening initialize as `initialize.<field>` (at most 40, lost first, each one line of about 64 characters at most); `kind` says what it costs: `lost` (the session does without something this invocation asked for — the informational warning names these), `kept` (an attach: the existing session keeps what it was created with) or `preference` (a display or host preference nobody would miss — the informational notice names these two), so a host may show them itself once or never; absent when nothing was left unapplied. `host`, when present, is what this machine announces as to the session: `handle` is the name the model addresses it by (and a client shows), `working_dir` the absolute directory served calls run in (that machine's separators), `platform` its platform word, `cli_version` its Claude Code version; each one line of at most 200 characters; present once this machine has built an announce for the session (bound, with something or an explicit nothing to serve), absent otherwise and on clients that predate it. `serving`, when present, says whether this machine serves its tools (Bash, Read, Write, Edit) to the session over the session's channel: `state` is `pending` while bound and about to announce, `on` once the session holds this machine's tools, `off` when it serves nothing, `revoked` when it stopped mid-session; `reason` (present when `state` is not `on` and the cause is known) is one of the client's serving-off keys — `not_bound` (see `device.reason`), `external_build`, `windows`, `muted` (Anthropic's emergency switch turned serving off; it comes back when the switch does), `switch_off`, `launched_from_home`, `channel_off`, `egress`, `policy_org` (the organization does not allow remote sessions), `flag_off`, `flag_stale`, `announce_refused`, `announce_unverified`, `superseded` — an open set: render an unrecognized value as a generic not-serving state; `policy` is the serving policy in effect (`parity`, or the stricter `interim` fallback); `channel` is `session`, or `bridge_only` when the session channel is switched off on this machine and served calls (if any) ride only the legacy device bridge, whose state this block does not describe. Absent on clients that predate it: feature-detect the key. `connection`, when present, is this client's stream to the session: `connecting` before it first connects, `live` while it is up, `reconnecting` while it is lost and being re-dialled (this machine is offline to the session meanwhile). `calls`, when present (once this machine has served a call this attach), is what it serves right now and how its last calls ended, by id and tool name only — never a call's input or output: `live` lists, oldest first, each call admitted here and not yet ended, `state` `running` while this machine executes it or `asked` while it waits on the session's approval (`ask_id` names the question; `since` is when it entered that state and `lapses_at` about when the session gives an unanswered question up, both epoch milliseconds on this machine's clock — the session's own timer decides); `recent` lists, newest last, at most 20 calls that ended here, `ended` being `completed`, `denied` (the session said no), `withdrawn` (the session took the question back unanswered — its patience ran out or the turn moved on), `refused` or `failed`, with `code` the result's disposition, refusal or failure word when it has one, and `at` when. `notices`, when present, is what this machine's serving has told the person during this attach that a host should show, at most 8: `key` is the notice's stable name (an open set — `device-mcp-consent`: this machine has MCP servers a cloud session could use and none are offered until the person allows it; `device-mcp-reconsent`: a server it offers changed the tools it lists and is withheld until re-approved, or this machine's record of what its servers list could not be read and none are offered — `text` says which; `device-mcp-policy`: a deny list in this machine's Claude Code settings lists remote-devices, so none of its MCP servers are offered; `device-mcp-dropped`; `served-hooks-not-run`; `served-hook-errors`; `served-bash-launched-from-home`; `served-tools-muted` / `served-tools-unmuted`; `announce_unverified`) and `text` its one line (at most 200 characters, no ANSI or newline) — this machine's own words with names from its own configuration, to be shown as plain text; written only by a serve-only helper (`--attach-serve`) and absent when nothing was said. `calls`, `connection` and `notices` are pushed between inits on `cloud_session_delta` frames. `client_version` rises only on a breaking change to this block — warn and continue on a higher value, never refuse; `not_applied[].kind`, `serving.state`, `connection`, `calls[].state` / `ended` and reason keys may gain values without it changing, so treat unrecognized values neutrally (an unrecognized `serving.state` as not serving — this schema itself parses an unrecognized `serving.state` as `off`, `policy` as `interim`, `channel` as `bridge_only`).

system_initOutput.description: Session metadata the CLI emits at the start of each turn, normally ahead of every other message of that turn: session_id, model, working directory, tools, MCP servers, slash commands, permission mode, and the capabilities list for feature detection.

total_chars.description: Combined length, in characters, of the instruction files in the session prompt: CLAUDE.md files, rules files and the files they import. Always over total_limit_chars.

total_limit_chars.description: The recommended limit for total_chars on the turn's model, in characters.

file_count.description: Number of files counted in total_chars. When it is 1, word the warning for a single file rather than a total.

largest_chars.description: Length of the largest file, in characters. Present only when the warning should mention it: there are several files and this one by itself is over total_limit_chars.

system_instruction_size_warningOutput.description: @internal The session's instruction files add up to more than the recommended limit. Numbers only: the host words the warning in the person's language. Sent to Claude Desktop's Code tab alone, at most once per process, on a conversation's first turn after system/init; never stored in the transcript. Safe to ignore: a host that does not recognize this subtype shows nothing.

system_local_command_outputOutput.description: Output from a local slash command (e.g. /voice, /usage). Displayed as assistant-style text in the transcript.

mode.description: How memories were surfaced: 'select' returns full file bodies chosen by the parallel selector; 'synthesize' returns a Sonnet-authored paragraph distilled from many tiny memories.

path.description: Absolute path to the memory file, a synthesis sentinel of the form `<synthesis:DIR>` when mode is 'synthesize', or an https URL when scope is 'organization'.

content.description: The surfaced memory body. Always present for 'synthesize' mode and 'organization' scope (neither has an on-disk path to lazy-load from); absent for file-backed 'select' entries (renderers lazy-load from path).

system_memory_recallOutput.description: Emitted when the memory recall supervisor surfaces relevant memories into the turn. Mirrors the CLI relevant_memories attachment so SDK renderers can show "Recalled from memory" inline.

system_mirror_errorOutput.description: Emitted when SessionStore.append() rejects or times out for a transcript-mirror batch after bounded retry (3 attempts with short backoff; timeouts are not retried). The batch is then dropped; this surfaces the failure so consumers are not silent on data loss.

scope.description: 'session': the main thread fell back and the session model is swapped. 'local': a subagent / side-question (/btw) / background fork fell back — only that response came from the fallback model and the session model is unchanged. Absent from older CLIs (treat as 'session').

api_refusal_category.description: The refusal category ('cyber', 'bio', …): stop_details.category from the refused API response (client lane), or the fallback block's server-gated trigger.category (server lane). Open string — new categories ship on the wire ahead of schema updates. null when neither source carried a category (normal, not an error). Absent when emitted by an older CLI.

saw_cyber_refusal.description: @internal Present when ANY hop of this banner's multi-hop episode was a cyber refusal — not only the origin hop that api_refusal_category describes (the banner keeps first-hop category semantics for display). Re-arm evidence for the CLI's cyber-exclusion header on session restore; never rendered, not part of the public SDK contract. Absent on cyber-free episodes and when emitted by an older CLI.

api_refusal_explanation.description: stop_details.explanation from the refused API response (client lane only — the server-lane trigger carries no explanation). Unstable human prose — display only, never parse. null/absent when the response carried none, and always null on server-lane banners.

retracted_message_uuids.description: Wire uuids of the messages this fallback retracted — the refused partial as the consumer received it (one uuid per normalized SDK message; multi-block messages carry per-block derived uuids) plus any tombstoned tool_results. Emitted AFTER the retraction, so this is a resolution-time eviction signal: remove these messages from transcript state on receipt. Eviction is idempotent — unknown or already-removed uuids are a no-op. Absent when emitted by an older CLI.

refused_user_message_uuid.description: UUID of the user message the refused request was for — the rewind target and composer prefill for edit-and-retry. This is the message's own uuid as delivered on the replay ack (not a per-block normalized uuid). null when the refused turn was not human-authored (e.g. a background task notification or auto-continuation — nothing to edit-and-retry) or otherwise cannot be identified; absent from older CLIs.

system_model_refusal_fallbackOutput.description: Emitted when the primary model ends the stream with stop_reason "refusal" and the turn is retried once on a fallback model (direction: "retry"). When `scope` is "session" (or absent — older CLIs), the swap is made persistent for the session; when `scope` is "local", only that subagent/side-question response came from the fallback model and the session model is unchanged. "revert" and "sticky" are retained in the enum for SDK-consumer compat and are no longer emitted.

system_model_refusal_no_fallbackOutput.description: Emitted when the model ends the stream with stop_reason "refusal" and no retry runs: no fallback model is configured, or per-category routing declined the retry (the mapped fallback target is unresolvable, or CLAUDE_CODE_REFUSAL_FALLBACK_CATCH_ALL is explicitly disabled and the refusal category has no fallback map entry). The structured counterpart to detecting stop_reason "refusal" on the assistant error frame. Not emitted when the retry ran or the user declined the retry dialog (model_refusal_fallback covers the retry case). Absent from older CLIs.

system_notificationOutput.description: Loop-side text notification. Mirrors the interactive REPL notification queue (key/priority/timeout). JSX notifications are not emitted on this channel.

state.description: 'held' when the receive-side policy parks the message instead of queueing it (once per message per hold cause — a re-announcement under a different cause emits again); then at most one of 'released' (the policy now accepts it: it enters the queue — its command_lifecycle 'queued' and, when it drains, its user replay echo follow under message_uuid) or 'dropped' (it will never reach the model in this session; see outcome).

message_uuid.description: The parked command's uuid — the value its later command_lifecycle frames and user replay echo carry. For lane 'bridge'/'stdin' it is the id the host (or its bridge) supplied on the inbound message; for lane 'socket' it was chosen by the SENDING session, so a host must correlate it only within peer_message_hold / peer replay frames, never against its own prompts' lifecycle.

lane.description: Which ingress delivered it: the Remote Control bridge, the host's own stdin stream, or the local cross-session socket.

from.description: The sender's address as the envelope will show it (the cross-session-message `from`) — an address-shaped token with control and invisible code points scrubbed; empty when the sender supplied none or an unshaped one. Sender-asserted on the socket lane: a label, not an identity proof.

from_name.description: The sender's display name when it supplied one, normalized and scrubbed the same way. A claim, like `from`.

cause.description: state 'held' only: why the policy parked it. 'mode-mismatch' / 'no-mode-asserted' are the permission-mode parity holds (the sender runs in a different permission class, or asserted none while this session bypasses permissions); the *-setting causes are a standing crossSessionInbound:'hold'.

outcome.description: state 'dropped' only: 'expired' — no one approved it before the approval deadline (a headless host has no approval surface, so every parity hold ends this way unless the mode changes first); 'refused' — the policy turned to refuse while it waited; 'dropped' — released or approved but the ingress guard (rate limit, duplicate, queue cap) discarded it; 'discarded' — the session ended with it still parked.

system_peer_message_holdOutput.description: @internal A cross-session (peer) message this session's receive-side policy HELD rather than queued, and how that hold resolved. Lets a host show the human that a message arrived but has not reached the model (and may never) instead of nothing at all; the sending session is told separately over its own transport where one exists. Informational only — there is no host-side approval through this frame. Emitted on the stdout stream in -p/SDK sessions.

per_turn_effort_active.description: Always false: a change to true is reported only by system/init.

system_per_turn_effort_changedOutput.description: @internal The conversation stopped sending effort per turn, because the server refused its per-turn effort message or a role:"system" message. From the retried request on, an effort change rewrites the cached prefix, for every model, until a later system/init says otherwise. Sent once, when the conversation first turns per-turn effort off, before the retried request's output, on the output stream of -p/SDK sessions; sent again only if the server refuses again after the conversation's refusals are cleared (for example by /clear or a compaction). It can repeat a false the host already holds. Pairs with system/init's per_turn_effort_active.

agent_id.description: Subagent ID when the tool call originated inside a subagent, as on permission_denied.

status.description: 'checking': the call has waited about four seconds on its check and is still waiting. 'done': that wait is over.

system_permission_check_statusOutput.description: @internal A tool call has been waiting on its automatic permission check (the auto-mode classifier) for longer than usual. It lets a host say that the step is being checked, where it would otherwise show a silent pause that looks like a running tool. Most checks answer within about four seconds and send nothing. The wait can include the rest of the model's streaming reply, or a dialog the host is showing about the check: prefer those indicators. Every 'checking' is followed by a 'done' for the same tool_use_id. 'done' does not say whether the call was allowed: the tool's result, permission_denied or a can_use_tool request does. One call can send more than one pair. Display-only and best-effort: a frame can be lost, so also stop showing it at any other frame for this tool_use_id or at the end of the turn. Emitted on the output stream of -p/SDK sessions.

agent_id.description: Subagent ID when the denied tool call originated inside a subagent. Mirrors can_use_tool for host-side routing.

decision_reason_code.description: @internal A closed-set code for a reason a host can act on, beside decision_reason_type (whose values are unchanged): 'outside_reads_blocked' (permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories refused the path), 'memory_paused' (memory is paused for the session), 'classifier_transcript_too_long' (the auto-mode classifier's transcript exceeded its context window). Absent for every other reason; new values are additive.

decision_reason.description: Human-readable reason from the deciding component, when available.

message.description: The rejection message returned to the model in the tool_result.

system_permission_deniedOutput.description: Emitted when a tool call is auto-denied without an interactive permission prompt (e.g. auto-mode classifier, dontAsk mode, headless-agent auto-deny, or a deny rule). With a permission prompt surface (stdio/SDK canUseTool), the 'ask' path surfaces via a can_use_tool control_request and this event covers the 'deny' short-circuit. Without one (bare -p / SDK query() with no canUseTool), 'ask' decisions are terminal, so this event also covers those implicit denials. Best-effort advisory: in rare races a denial can book without a frame or a frame can lack a booking twin — result.permission_denials is the authoritative record. Denials that resolve before canUseTool runs — PreToolUse hook denies, deny-rule overrides of hook allow/ask decisions, and file-tool calls (Read, Edit, Write) refused by a path-scoped deny rule — are not covered here, and neither is the MCP --permission-prompt-tool surface (the prompt tool is the host there).

system_plugin_installOutput.description: Headless plugin installation progress (CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_PLUGIN_INSTALL). started/completed bracket the whole install; installed/failed carry a per-marketplace name.

system_post_turn_summaryOutput.description: @internal Background post-turn summary emitted after each assistant turn. summarizes_uuid points to the assistant message this summarizes.

system_session_metadataOutput.description: @internal The same external_metadata patch a cloud worker sends the session server, for the keys a local host needs: today `artifacts` (the session's published-artifact list, whole list on each change, null once empty). Lets an SDK host keep the per-session summary a cloud session gets, without reading transcript rows.

system_session_state_changedOutput.description: Mirrors notifySessionStateChanged. 'idle' fires after heldBackResult flushes and the bg-agent do-while exits — authoritative turn-over signal.

title.description: The session's current name. Control, bidirectional and zero-width characters are replaced with single spaces, the ends are trimmed, and the name is at most 200 Unicode code points. When another session already has the name, a suffix can make it unique.

system_session_title_changedOutput.description: @internal The session's name, for a host that shows it, such as an IDE editor tab. A headless (print mode) session sends it at startup when the session already has a name, and again after each change to the name (not an AI-generated title), including a rename the host itself sent with `rename_session`. A name that another process writes to the transcript arrives when this process next reads the end of its transcript: after about 32 KB of its own transcript writes, or at a compaction. A cleared name is not sent. The same name can arrive more than once, for example when it is set again, so a host should treat a repeated name as no change. The frame can arrive before the system/init message that first names its session_id, for example at startup or after /clear. A host that learns the session id from system/init can hold the name until then.

permissionMode.description: Permission mode for controlling how tool executions are handled. 'default' - Standard behavior, prompts for dangerous operations. 'acceptEdits' - Auto-accept file edit operations. 'bypassPermissions' - Bypass all permission checks (requires allowDangerouslySkipPermissions). 'plan' - Planning mode, no actual tool execution. 'dontAsk' - Don't prompt for permissions, deny if not pre-approved. 'auto' - Use a model classifier to approve/deny permission prompts.

compact_output_chars.description: @internal On the 'compacting' statuses of an automatic compaction (absent on a typed /compact): characters of the summary streamed so far (text and tool-input deltas, not thinking). Returns to 0 at each new attempt at the summary (a request retried inside an attempt adds to what the dropped try streamed), and stays 0 while waiting for a summary written in the background. A rising count shows that the summary is being written; a still one proves nothing, and it is not a share of the final length, which is not known in advance.

run_id.description: Id of one run of the task: equal on every task_* event, background_tasks_changed entry and saved notification (its origin.runId) of that run. A resumed task keeps its task_id and gets a new one. The run ids of one task sort, by plain string comparison, in the order the runs opened; a frame that names a run sorting before the one a reader shows is late. Nothing else about the format is promised. Absent for a task this process did not register, and from CLIs that predate it.

reason.description: Machine-readable cause, set only when the task did not end through an ordinary completion, failure, or stop. 'worker_restart': the worker process restarted and the resumed process found the task orphaned (always with status 'stopped').

resource_links.description: CLI-owned: for a backgrounded MCP task (task_type mcp_task) that completed, the `resource_link` content blocks of its final result — the files it returned by reference — collected from the raw result before the CLI renders it as the text the model reads. A backgrounded task's tool_result is the placeholder text and its real result arrives as this notification, so this is where a host learns which files that tool call produced; join to the originating call via tool_use_id. Same fields and caps as tool_use_result.resourceLinks (at most 50 links, 64 KiB serialized), absent when the result had none or the task is any other type. Never populated from the server's _meta.

handback.description: @internal Present on a 'completed' notification of a subagent that reports through the SubagentHandback tool: how its report reached its caller, with the values and meaning of `handback` on AgentToolCompletedOutput. Left out when the subagent failed, was stopped, is waiting on agents it started, or is waiting on its own background work with nothing delivered yet; for such a subagent, `summary` is then not a report. When present, `summary` holds harness notes written for the model. Any notification can be followed by a later one for the same task_id when the agent is resumed or finishes its wait; the later one replaces what the earlier one showed.

text.description: The subagent's whole report, never truncated, with a backslash inserted into text that imitates harness markup, such as a system tag (`<system-reminder>`), a `[harness:` line or a turn marker (`Human:` at the start of a line)

warning.description: Auto mode's warning to show above `text`: a SECURITY WARNING, or a note that the review could not run

handback_report.description: @internal The report a 'send' or 'flagged' hand-back delivered, the same shape as `handbackReport` on AgentToolCompletedOutput: when present, render it instead of `summary`, with its `warning`, if it has one, above its `text`. Absent for 'withheld'; if it is absent for another value too, show `summary`.

ambient.description: True for tasks that are not activity (every skip_transcript task, plus every live-update watcher, requested or auto-started); hosts should exclude them from activity indicators.

run_id.description: Id of one run of the task: equal on every task_* event, background_tasks_changed entry and saved notification (its origin.runId) of that run. A resumed task keeps its task_id and gets a new one. The run ids of one task sort, by plain string comparison, in the order the runs opened; a frame that names a run sorting before the one a reader shows is late. Nothing else about the format is promised. Absent for a task this process did not register, and from CLIs that predate it.

subagent_type.description: Subagent type for Task tool subagents.

summary.description: A one-line status for the task's row. For a local_agent task it is the model-generated progress summary (only when the agentProgressSummaries option is on); for a backgrounded mcp_task it is the MCP server's own bounded status message, emitted once per change without any option. Render it when present regardless of task type.

run_id.description: Id of one run of the task: equal on every task_* event, background_tasks_changed entry and saved notification (its origin.runId) of that run. A resumed task keeps its task_id and gets a new one. The run ids of one task sort, by plain string comparison, in the order the runs opened; a frame that names a run sorting before the one a reader shows is late. Nothing else about the format is promised. Absent for a task this process did not register, and from CLIs that predate it.

subagent_type.description: Subagent type for Task tool subagents.

is_backgrounded.description: Whether the task was registered in the background (true) or in the foreground with the spawning tool call blocking on it (false). A resumed subagent is always registered in the background. A later move to the background arrives as task_updated patch.is_backgrounded. Set for local_agent and local_bash tasks.

awaited.description: @internal True for a run of a resumed subagent (local_agent) that the tool call which resumed it waits for, as SendMessage does when background tasks are disabled; its task_started, if one is sent, names that call in tool_use_id. The run has ended by the time that call returns or throws, even when the wait is aborted. Its report goes into that call's result, so expect no follow-up turn when it ends. A later resume that nothing waits for starts a new run without the field.

spawn_depth.description: Nesting depth of a spawned subagent (local_agent) task: 1 for a top-level spawn, N+1 when spawned from inside a depth-N agent. Not set on other tasks.

parent_task_id.description: task_id of the subagent (local_agent) task whose agent launched this subagent, shell, monitor or workflow task. Absent when the launcher is the main thread, has no task_id of its own (a teammate, an agent inside a workflow), or is no longer tracked. A resumed subagent keeps its original parent. The parent may be a foreground or already-ended task, so treat an unknown id as no parent.

workflow_name.description: meta.name from the workflow script (e.g. 'spec'). Only set when task_type is 'local_workflow'.

skip_transcript.description: Ambient/housekeeping task. Consumers should hide this from the inline transcript; it may still appear in a tasks panel.

ambient.description: True for tasks that are not activity (every skip_transcript task, plus every live-update watcher, requested or auto-started); hosts should exclude them from activity indicators.

system_task_summaryOutput.description: @internal Mid-turn progress line from the debounced classifier. Mirrors external_metadata.task_summary so non-CCR consumers (desktop LocalSessionManager) see the same live phrase. detail is null on the idle clear.

run_id.description: Id of one run of the task: equal on every task_* event, background_tasks_changed entry and saved notification (its origin.runId) of that run. A resumed task keeps its task_id and gets a new one. The run ids of one task sort, by plain string comparison, in the order the runs opened; a frame that names a run sorting before the one a reader shows is late. Nothing else about the format is promised. Absent for a task this process did not register, and from CLIs that predate it.

patch.description: Wire-safe subset of TaskState fields that changed. Excludes abortController, messages, result. Clients merge into their local task map.

user_message_uuid.description: Client uuid of the user message that triggered this turn (submitMessage options.uuid), stamped on every thinking_tokens frame of a headless (stream-json / Agent SDK) turn so a consumer can attribute thinking progress to the send it answers before any reply frame arrives. On a synthetic/scheduled (meta) turn it names the last user message folded into the turn so far once one has been, else the turn's own uuid when the host vouches it is the client event's own (delivered content such as a Slack owner ping). Absent on turns that neither had a client uuid nor folded a user message in, on Remote Control (interactive terminal) sessions, and from older producers.

system_thinking_tokensOutput.description: Live thinking-token estimate, digested from thinking_delta.estimated_tokens during the redacted-thinking phase (where the API otherwise streams only pings). estimated_tokens is the running total for the current thinking block; estimated_tokens_delta is the increment carried by this frame. Approximate progress for spinners/pills, not the authoritative billed output_tokens.

staged_files.description: @internal Present, and true, when this worker starts a handed-off turn's calls only after every stage_file control request it received earlier has finished or failed, or a wait limit has passed; a worker that omits it may start them while files are still downloading. Exception: a request with filestore_path set (a synced file) is not waited for, so a call that names that file may start before it is synced.

no_query_first.description: @internal True when user messages with shouldQuery false that reach this worker before a turn_handoff request are appended, and acknowledged, before the handed-off turn produces any output. Exception: a request that continues a turn whose leading lines an earlier request appended; that turn goes first. A worker that omits it may run the turn first.

shared_message_id.description: @internal True when this worker accepts a turn_handoff request in which an assistant message repeats the message id of the assistant message before it, as the messages member of that request describes. A worker that omits it refuses such a request (invalid_handoff), so a client gives each message an id of its own there.

relay_marker.description: @internal Present, and true, only when this worker uses the relay_marker member of a turn_handoff request; a client sends that member to no other worker.

home_files.description: @internal Present, and true, only on a worker that takes a stage_file control request whose mount_path is /uploads/.home/<path> as a file for /home/claude/<path>: it writes the file there, answers ok with a noop (already_present, path_occupied, refused_name, home_files_off, unchecked_announcement, resent_announcement) and writes nothing, or answers an error. Any other worker treats that path as an ordinary upload.

file_names.description: @internal Present, and true, only when this worker uses the file_names member of a turn_handoff request; a client sends that member to no other worker.

carried_writes.description: @internal Present, and true, only on a worker that writes the files of the Write calls a turn_handoff request brings already answered, where their paths are under /home/claude. Before it appends a turn that has calls to run, it writes each such call's content to its path, replacing nothing. If it cannot write them all, it appends and runs nothing: the request is refused with an error that starts "invalid_handoff: carried_writes_", or it is accepted and the turn ends in a result with num_turns 0. Any other worker writes no file for these calls.

hydrates_carried_lines.description: @internal Present, and true, only on a worker that rebuilt the conversation from the session's stored transcript before it read any request, and would not have started without it. A client may send this worker again a turn_handoff request that an earlier worker accepted, if the request names no calls (tool_use_ids empty), is not stopped, and its messages hold no tool call. A request whose turn had not ended when an earlier worker with this key stopped is left unacknowledged, so the session service sends it to this worker by itself; a second request for the same turn is answered "duplicate" while the first waits or runs. The worker appends only the messages of the turn that its conversation lacks and, once the store has confirmed every message of the turn, sends the turn's last message back as an assistant event (the echo); a turn it already holds whole is echoed on the same condition. The request can still be accepted, or refused ("invalid_handoff:"), with no echo, and the turn may then not be stored. That happens, for example, when the conversation has moved on past the part of the turn it holds, when a rewind has removed the turn, when a compaction has summarised part of it (or all of it, if the compaction was this worker's own), when a Stop clears the queue first, or when the store does not confirm the messages. A request sent again waits again for messages not yet confirmed. When a delivery finds that the store refused a message of the turn, it sends no echo and removes the turn from the conversation, and the same request sent again to that worker gets no echo. If another row has followed the turn, the turn stays, also with no echo. Exception: after 512 later refused rows the worker forgets a refusal and reads the message as confirmed. Confirmed means that the store answered the upload with success. A turn that an earlier worker's compaction summarised whole is appended a second time. The key promises nothing for a turn that holds a tool call, or whose first message is stored with no answer but with another row behind it (a hook's output, say): the worker may already have continued such a turn itself when it started. A worker without the key may have started with none of the turn's messages.

requires_rewind_request_id.description: @internal Present, and true, only on a worker that reads the requires_rewind_request_id member of a turn_handoff request; a worker without this key ignores the member and appends the turn whether or not the rewind was made.

system_turn_handoff_availableOutput.description: @internal Emitted once by a cloud worker that accepts the turn_handoff control request, after it registers, carrying what it wrote to external_metadata.turn_handoff: the version, the tools whose calls it would accept, the worker life (worker_epoch) announcing it, whether handed-off calls wait for files still being staged (staged_files), whether user messages that make no model call are appended before a handed-off turn (no_query_first), whether two assistant messages of a turn may share a message id (shared_message_id), whether a turn_handoff request may name a rewind it depends on (requires_rewind_request_id), and relay_marker, home_files, file_names, carried_writes and hydrates_carried_lines when set. Lets a session client learn the capability from the event stream instead of reading worker state. Durable in the stream: a reader keeps the entry with the newest worker_epoch it has seen and ignores older ones; a worker life that does not accept turn_handoff emits nothing (its registration writes turn_handoff: null).

reason.description: Why the turn was stopped. 'rapid_followup': the user's next message arrived before the running turn showed any output. More reasons may be added; treat an unknown one the same way.

preempted_by_uuid.description: The client-supplied uuid of the queued user message the turn was stopped for. It runs next, together with any messages queued behind it.

preempted_message_uuids.description: The client-supplied uuids of the user messages the stopped turn was running (uuid-less members omitted; may be empty).

system_turn_preemptedOutput.description: @internal The CLI itself stopped the running turn so a user's rapid follow-up message is answered at once, exactly as a priority 'now' message would have (running shell commands are backgrounded, not killed). Sent at the moment of the stop, so it precedes the stopped turn's result frame (terminal_reason aborted_streaming or aborted_tools) and its members' 'cancelled' command_lifecycle frames (it can also precede the follow-up's own 'queued' command_lifecycle frame): a host renders that turn as superseded by the follow-up rather than as interrupted, does not resend its messages, and treats only preempted_by_uuid as picked up. At most one per burst: the turn the follow-up starts is never preempted this way. Emitted on the stdout stream in -p/SDK sessions only, and only to a consumer that declared rapidFollowupPreempt on its initialize request, while the feature's rollout flag is on: without both, the turn is not stopped at all. Explicit 'now' and 'later' priorities never produce it.

component.description: @internal Which site: a pane's body or the band.

system_ui_focusOutput.description: @internal Fire-and-forget push when a plugin's `$.ui.focus` (through the `ui.focus` chain) moved the focus ring of a site a remote surface draws onto one of its Buttons, Inputs or Selects: the surface focuses that element if it still draws it. The person's own moves (ui_focus requests) are never pushed back.

event.description: @internal The render event whose version moved; the engine versions `ui.render` as one event, so no component or instance is named.

prompts_screened.description: @internal Present while a mod may change what is recorded of a typed line (a hook on `prompt.submit`, `command.run`, `session.append` or, for a line sent to the session, `session.receive`; mods not yet known; or an organization policy that lists a plugin or cannot be read): what the `prompts_screened_v1` capability says on `system/init`, said as soon as a plugin load or reload makes it so. Absent says nothing: the next `system/init` does.

surface.description: @internal The surface that drew the instance.

instance_id.description: @internal The engine's requestId of the instance, as the ui_render that drew it named it.

instances.description: @internal Present when a plugin wrote state (`$.state.set`) that these instances read while they were drawn, or a `Client` drawn in them failed and its plugin heard it (`ui.fault`), and nothing else moved: only they are stale, and the surface may re-ask them alone. Absent, every mounted instance may be stale, as before. A surface that ignores the field re-asks everything and stays correct.

system_ui_invalidateOutput.description: @internal Fire-and-forget push from the hooks engine when a plugin called `$.ui.invalidate("ui.render")` or a plugin loaded or reloaded: every tree a remote surface drew through ui_render may be stale. The surface re-asks each mounted instance; the engine dedups the evaluations. Bumps from one plugin fold to at most one per 100 ms. With `instances`, a state write or a `Client` that failed made only those stale.

plugin.description: @internal The calling plugin's registry name, as the hooks engine knows it (never plugin-settable).

text.description: @internal The line the plugin gave: be ready for up to 10000 characters of it and then an ellipsis. Plain text: draw it as a text node, never as markup.

system_ui_logOutput.description: @internal Fire-and-forget push from a headless session for one `$.ui.log(text)` line: what the REPL appends to its transcript as a dim notice under the plugin's name. Not sent to the model. Lines are not counted across the session: a plugin's lines are the plugin's to write, however long the session runs; ones logged before the stream opened are delivered first, in order.

id.description: @internal A pane's id as the plugin opened it (`$.ui.open({ id })`): 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `_`, `-`. What a ui_render for `Pane` carries as `instance_id`.

title.description: @internal The pane's tab label: the `title` its latest open gave, else its id. Plugin-authored text the engine bounded and freed of control characters: draw it as a text node, never as markup.

plugin.description: @internal The registry name of the plugin that opened it, as the engine knows it; a `$.ui.scroll` or `$.ui.focus` of the pane is that plugin's alone.

close_on_escape.description: @internal Escape while the pane holds the keyboard, or at an idle empty composer, closes it as the person's close does (send ui_close); absent, Escape only returns the keyboard.

hold_toasts.description: @internal The surface holds its transient toasts while this pane is the one shown, and shows them once it closes.

background_color.description: @internal What the surface paints under this pane's body while it is the one shown: a theme key, a raw color, or `transparent` for nothing; checked at open, yet parse it, never write it into a style. Absent, the surface's own look stands.

rows.description: @internal The body rows its content asked for while seated inline; a request the person's own sizing overrides.

columns.description: @internal The body columns its content asked for while docked; a request the person's own sizing overrides.

items.description: @internal One placed pane as the engine holds it (plugins/functionHooks/panes/): which, its tab, its opener, and the manners and size its latest open asked for.

panes.description: @internal The placed open panes in open order (an open appends, a close removes); a pane waiting unplaced is not listed. The surface draws one container for them: tabs when several, the shown one visible.

anyOf.description: @internal A pane's id as the plugin opened it (`$.ui.open({ id })`): 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `_`, `-`. What a ui_render for `Pane` carries as `instance_id`.

focus_requested_id.description: @internal A standing `$.ui.open({ focus: true })` the surface has yet to judge: honour it (focus the pane, send ui_pane_focus with its id) only while the composer is empty and idle and no dialog is up, else refuse it (ui_pane_focus with null).

system_ui_panesOutput.description: @internal Fire-and-forget push from a headless session whenever the pane roster a remote surface draws changes: a plugin opened, retitled or closed a pane, the person showed, focused or closed one, a placing client attached. Deduplicated: an unchanged roster is not pushed. A pane opened before the stream armed produces none; read the roster with ui_panes on mount.

text.description: @internal The plugin's pinned line, replacing its previous one; null removes it. Be ready for up to 10000 characters of it and then an ellipsis. Plain text: draw it as a text node, never as markup.

system_ui_statusOutput.description: @internal Fire-and-forget push from a headless session for one `$.ui.status(text)`: the line the REPL pins under the prompt beside the engine's own notices until the plugin's next call replaces or clears it.

text.description: @internal The line the plugin gave: be ready for up to 10000 characters of it and then an ellipsis. Plain text: draw it as a text node, never as markup.

timeout_ms.description: @internal How long the REPL would keep it on the notification bar: the plugin's `timeoutMs`, or the engine's default (4000).

system_ui_toastOutput.description: @internal Fire-and-forget push from a headless session for one `$.ui.toast(text)`: what the REPL shows on the notification bar under the prompt for a few seconds, under the plugin's name. Be ready for a plugin's toasts at no fixed rate; nothing counts how many a plugin has shown.

kind.description: What class of mutation was observed. New kinds may be added — treat an unrecognized kind exactly like a recognized one (something changed, go look).

cwd.description: The directory the shell was in when the command finished (so an inner cd is reflected; a git -C target is not) — a hint about where to look, never proof of what moved: confirm against the repository itself.

branch.description: The branch a commit landed on (from the commit summary line git prints per commit) or a push updated (from the ref-update line git prints per pushed ref, e.g. `HEAD -> other`). Commit and push events carry it; a command that pushed several branches emits one push event per branch. A best-effort hint: absent whenever attribution is uncertain (a push whose output was redirected still emits, with no branch; a push that also updated a ref whose name could not be carried emits a nameless event beside the named ones), and never a required key.

system_vcs_state_changedOutput.description: @internal A harness-observed shell command mutated repository state (git commit/cherry-pick, push, merge, rebase — dry runs excluded). A cache-invalidation signal with a deliberately minimal payload: beyond classification it carries the branch acted on and the directory the shell finished in, both hints about where to look, so consumers still re-read state (head, PR status) from the repository instead of decoding the event. Derived from the same detection as the tool result's structured gitOperation data, so the two agree on what happened; only a push's `branch` is attributed more strictly here (from the push's own output section) than in that data. A compound command can emit more than one kind (a merge and a rebase in one command collapse to the latter), and a push of several branches emits one push event per branch; coalesce freely. Best-effort, not exhaustive: only foreground mutations run through the Bash/PowerShell tools are observed — a backgrounded command whose confirming output had not printed at capture time emits nothing. A foreground push whose ref lines were redirected or silenced still emits, on the invoking command's zero exit code alone (so a compound that swallows a failed push's code also emits; the event is a prompt to look, never a claim).

reason.description: Short snake_case reason set by the host CLI (not user input), e.g. 'host_exit', 'remote_control_disabled'.

system_worker_shutting_downOutput.description: Emitted by the bridge on opt-in graceful worker teardown (only when the teardown caller supplied a reason), before the heartbeat stops, so remote clients can show why the worker went away instead of waiting for heartbeat timeout. Absence is NOT a dead-host signal: handoffs (/update, /teleport, respawn), auto-disable, mode transitions, and internal fatal-error paths emit nothing by design. A dead host (battery, OOM, kill -9) never reaches teardown and never sends this either. NOTE: this event lands in the durable per-session event stream — a session that is later resumed may carry historical instances mid-stream. Clients MUST treat it as a live-tail signal only (honored when no further activity follows), not a one-shot session-lifetime fact.

timestamp.description: @internal ISO timestamp when the summary was created on the originating process. From internal ToolUseSummaryMessage.timestamp.

items.description: A request content block. text, image, document, search_result, tool_use, tool_result and thinking blocks are modelled; the other API block types are accepted by type tag only, and consumers must tolerate types newer than this list.

content.description: A bare string (shorthand for one text block) or a list of content blocks.

message.description: An Anthropic Messages API user message: a MessageParam with role "user" whose content is a string or an array of content blocks (text, image, document, tool_result, ...). See the Messages API reference for the block types.

tool_use_result.description: Structured tool output — the tool's full Output object, not the string content sent to the model. The shape is per-tool, keyed by the matching tool_use block's name (see the *Output types in toolTypes); MCP and dynamic tools carry their own shapes, so the field stays unknown-typed. For the Agent/Task tool the completed shape is the subagent's final report without the model-directed agentId/usage trailer, plus run totals — render from it instead of parsing the tool_result text. A call that stepped aside for a message the user sent (today a WebFetch or WebSearch call) carries `{ detachedToolCall: true }` in place of its Output: the call is still running, and its result reaches the model in a later turn.

requeue_if_interrupted_within_ms.description: @internal Input only. Asks the CLI to put this prompt back in its queue, instead of losing it, when an interrupt crosses with a running turn taking the prompt in: the interrupt was sent while its sender still believed the prompt was waiting. The value says for how long an interrupt is taken to have been sent so: a whole number of milliseconds from 1, and above 10000 it counts as 10000. The time runs from the moment the turn announces the model request that carries the prompt (system/status 'requesting', which is on the wire only with partial messages); until then it has not begun. The prompt is put back when an interrupt control request without cancel_queued stops that turn within the time and before the model's next reply has begun to arrive. It goes back to the front of the queue under the same uuid and runs in a later turn of its own, after any queued prompt of higher priority; prompts queued behind it are not merged into that turn's prompt, though the turn can take them in as any turn does. The interrupt's response lists it under still_queued and under put_back, and from then on cancel_async_message can withdraw it. The stopped turn reports no 'cancelled' for it, counts it in its result's queued_turn_count (if its origin is stamped user-driven, as for any queued prompt) and leaves it out of that result's user_message_uuids (on an error result an empty list, with no user_message_uuid, if nothing else is listed). On stdout it reports command_lifecycle 'queued' a second time; over a remote transport its delivery is not reported 'processed' until its later turn ends. With cancel_queued:true it stays with the stopped turn and is not listed under the response's cancelled. The row the stopped turn wrote for it (a queued_command attachment) leaves the conversation and is never stored, so the model sees the prompt once; until the prompt can no longer be put back, that row and the rows after it are kept out of the stored transcript. UserPromptSubmit hooks run for it twice, and what they added to the stopped turn stays. If a compaction begins while that row is kept out, the row is stored at once and stays in the conversation, so the prompt, if an interrupt puts it back or has just done so, is seen twice. A prompt is put back at most once, and never after the host's own cancel_async_message for it answered cancelled:false. Of several prompts taken in since the model last spoke, only the last can be put back; the others stay with the stopped turn. The field is ignored when it is not such a number, when the message has no uuid or has shouldQuery:false, and when the message is not a person's own typing: a synthetic, hidden, client-composed, seeded, peer or relayed message, one that declares a non-human origin, or one whose client_platform names no app or keyboard that a person types in. claude-code-server also needs a client_platform, and one that names an app. A CLI that does not advertise interrupt_requeue_taken_v1 on system/init ignores the field too.

fromMode.description: The SENDING session's permission class as declared by the host that injects this message on local stdin ('bypass' for sessions that run tools without asking, 'prompting' otherwise). Lets the recipient deliver a same-class message immediately while a cross-class or undeclared sender is still held at a recipient that runs without asking. Honored only from the injecting host on local stdin; absent when the host does not declare it.

name.description: Sender display name, normalized by the harness: Unicode control, format, surrogate, and line/paragraph-separator code points stripped (categories Cc/Cf/Cs/Zl/Zp — covers bidi controls, zero-width characters, and tag characters), trimmed, at most 64 code points (+ ellipsis, never splitting a surrogate pair). Sender-asserted display text (the addressable identity is `from`) — render it as reported speech, but no client-side character sanitization is needed. Absent when the wire is not exactly one harness-formed envelope and on messages from older senders.

fromSession.description: The sender's host-openable session id (the envelope's `from-session` attribute — e.g. a desktop `local_<uuid>` or a cloud session `session_`/`ses_` id), set by the sender's host so a receiving UI can link this message back to the sending session. Sender-asserted like `from`: a navigation target only, never authority. Absent when the sender's host provides none and on messages from older senders.

inbound_origin.description: @internal Server-asserted ingest path of the demoted delivery, copied at classification from the message-level `inbound_origin`.

senderTaskId.description: Task id of the in-process background subagent that sent this message, stamped by the harness from the sending loop (never from tool input). Absent for cross-session peers.

body.description: Decoded message body with the peer envelope stripped — byte-exact with what the model sees. Present only when the turn is exactly one harness-formed envelope (or an in-process agent message); render this instead of re-parsing the message text.

verifiedPeerPid.description: Kernel-verified pid of the process that connected to this session's cross-session messaging socket, read from the connection (SO_PEERCRED / LOCAL_PEERPID) — never from the payload. This identifies the CONNECTING process, which for relayed traffic (e.g. a daemon forwarding on another session's behalf) is the relay, not the message's author. Key sender identity on this, never on `from`: `from` is sender-authored and kept only for reply routing, so it is forgeable by any same-user process. Absent when unverifiable (Windows, non-UDS ingress) — never a wrong value. Pids are recyclable: provenance, not an authentication token.

handback.description: @internal Present, and always true, when the message is a subagent's final report to the agent that launched it, delivered through the SubagentHandback tool. Stamped by the harness, never from tool input. `body` is then the hand-back frame line with the indented report under it, and any harness note above it; `handbackReportText` and `handbackNote` carry those two parts for display. A boolean mark: not the `handback` state string of a task notification or of an Agent tool result. A hand-back is never joined, so neither this mark nor `flagged` appears beside `members`.

flagged.description: @internal Present, and always true, on a hand-back that auto mode's review blocked, or that it could not judge because a safety filter refused the review request: the report was delivered all the same, under the SECURITY WARNING that `handbackNote` carries. Never cap or fold such a message: show the note and the report in full. Absent on a hand-back that was not flagged, including one delivered under the note that the review was unavailable.

handbackNote.description: @internal On a hand-back: the note the harness composed above the frame line in `body`, without the indent. On a blocked report it quotes the review's reason, which can quote the report, so show it as untrusted text. Absent when there is no note.

handbackReportText.description: @internal On a hand-back: the subagent's report as the model reads it, under the frame line in `body`, without the indent. Draw it as a separate element from `handbackNote`: the two fields are their only boundary. Absent wherever `body` is and on a message that is not a hand-back.

members.description: @internal On a prompt that joins several queued messages from this sender: the joined messages in the order the model reads them, each with its own `body`. The origin's `body` is then absent. Absent on a message that was not joined and when any joined message had no `body`.

subkind.description: Present when the delivery is the fired stored prompt of a scheduled task/routine ('scheduled-trigger', stamped from server-asserted provenance, or declared by a local host for its own scheduled runs; the schedule attests storage, not authorship) or a coordinator co-member SendMessage delivery ('peer-send-message': model-authored text from another of the same user's sessions, verified by the server-stamped receiver co-membership — task-notification for prompt authority, but distinguishable so the receive-side crossSessionInbound setting can apply to it). The harness frames a scheduled-trigger delivery as the session's assigned task instead of the generic background-notification frame. Absent on webhook, PR-steward, plugin, and background-event deliveries.

fireReason.description: On a 'scheduled-trigger' delivery, why it fired: a short lowercase token such as 'scheduled', 'manual', 'retry', 'catch_up' or 'api'. Set by the server for cloud routines, or declared by a local host for its own scheduled runs, which is honored only in a process the host started with CLAUDE_CODE_HOST_SCHEDULED_RUN=1 (a local host's value is kept only if it is 1 to 32 lowercase letters or underscores); absent when neither sent one.

producer.description: @internal Present ('session-task') when the notification reports on work this session itself launched: a background agent, shell command, workflow, monitor, MCP or remote task settling, a detached tool call, or a hook rewake or worker check-in following up on such work. Absent on webhook, artifact and other externally-authored deliveries.

runId.description: On a background task's own notification: the run_id its task_* events carried, as of when the notification was queued. Not part of the text the model reads.

taskKind.description: @internal Present ('mcp-task') only on a notification that an MCP server's own task has ended, and not on every one. Narrower than task_type 'mcp_task', which also covers an MCP tool call moved to the background.

oneOf.description: Injected turn whose ingress classification found no provenance. Framed by the harness as a non-user source in both drains; never presumed human, never host-replayed.
Report from a background observer agent to the agent it observes. One-way by construction — the observed agent must not reply.
Activity digest delivered to an observer agent. The message body is the self-framing digest (envelope + postamble); observed content is data, not instructions.

origin.description: Provenance of a user-role message (peer session, team lead, channel). A host wrapping keyboard input must stamp {kind:'human'} explicitly — absent origin is treated as unattributed and fails closed at strict isHuman() trust gates.

client_platform.description: @internal The `anthropic-client-platform` value of the client that sent this message (e.g. `ios`, `android`, `web_claude_ai`, `desktop_app`). Injected server-side by CCR ingress from the request header.

inbound_origin.description: @internal Server-asserted ingest path that produced this message. Not settable by clients.

server_received_wall_ms.description: @internal Epoch ms on the session server's clock when it received the HTTP request that delivered this message. Written by the session server; the CLI copies it to the turn's result as user_message_server_received_wall_ms.

historical.description: @internal Replayed history rather than a live message: the Remote Control bridge stamps it on the messages it flushes to the session server, which also stamps it on deliveries it replays.

shouldQuery.description: When false, the message is appended to the transcript without triggering an assistant turn. It will be merged into the next user message that does query.

timestamp.description: ISO timestamp when the message was created on the originating process. Older emitters omit it; consumers should fall back to receive time.

is_meta.description: @internal True when the message was synthesized by the loop (not user keyboard input). From internal UserMessage.isMeta.

seeded_summon.description: @internal Desktop host only: the host's own seeded summon.

client_composed.description: The client composed this turn from content the user did not type; the CLI delivers its text as written, with no `@path` file-mention expansion and no slash-command dispatch. On current CLIs the turn-start attachment pass is skipped as a whole: `@server:resource` MCP mentions are not expanded either, and the prompt is sent without the context the CLI normally attaches alongside it (nested `CLAUDE.md` and rules files, skill and tool listings, reminders); the pass the CLI runs between tool calls is unaffected.

text_not_typed.description: @internal No person typed this message's text in this session (a server or an app composed it). The text is delivered as written and is not treated as typing: no slash-command dispatch, no at-mention expansion beyond the message's own uploaded files, no reminder or command from keywords in it, and a skill named in it does not count as typed by the user. Who sent the message, and whether a person is present, stays with its origin. The checks of whether a message's words are the user's own do not read this mark yet: they too go by the origin. Unlike client_composed, the turn-start attachment pass still runs. Any value other than false or null is read as true.

initiator.description: @internal The host's own label for what started this turn (e.g. the desktop app's `scheduled-task`, `sleep-auto-resume`); `user` or absent means a person sent it. Usage attribution only; it does not change how the turn runs.

is_visible_in_transcript_only.description: @internal True when the message is stored in the transcript but not rendered in the live UI.

is_virtual.description: @internal Display-only: rendered in the UI but filtered before API send.

is_compact_summary.description: @internal True when this user message is a compact-summary synthetic message.

summarize_metadata.description: @internal Metadata for "Summarize from here" / "Summarize up to here" summaries (from internal UserMessage.summarizeMetadata).

resource_links.description: CLI-owned: the `resource_link` content blocks the MCP tool returned, collected from the raw result before the CLI rewrites each into the `[Resource link: NAME] URI` text line the model reads — so a host renders the files without parsing that line. At most 50 links and 64 KiB serialized; absent when the result had none, and absent on a subagent's tool results (parent_tool_use_id set), whose mcpMeta carries `_meta` only. On today's wire this rides the mcpMeta spread as `tool_use_result.resourceLinks`. A sibling of `_meta`, never inside it: a server cannot supply it, and server `_meta` keys under the CLI-reserved `com.anthropic/` prefix are dropped before this message.

mcp_meta.description: @internal MCP protocol metadata passed through to SDK consumers, never sent to the model (from internal UserMessage.mcpMeta).

servers.description: mcp_needs_auth / mcp_disabled: the server names as configured. mcp_required_missing: the name patterns the agent definition requires that no connected server matches.

provider.description: auth_expired / auth_overridden / auth_missing_scope / design_needs_authorization: whose login the fix names — 'claude_ai' (the claude.ai account, /login) or 'claude_design' (Claude Design's own authorization, /design login).

path.description: outside_reads_blocked: the path the read block refused, when the refusal names one. staged_for_review: the settings file the write was held for.

managed.description: outside_reads_blocked: an organization policy sets the block, so the user cannot remove it. auth_overridden: the overriding credential was injected by the host environment, so nothing in this session can unset it.

feature.description: feature_disabled / policy_denied: the feature that is off.

cause.description: feature_disabled: why the feature is off — 'managed_settings' (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS, or disableWorkflows or enableWorkflows: false set by a layer above the user's own settings), 'org_policy', 'unavailable' (not launched for this account), 'user_setting' (the user's /config setting is off, including a disableWorkflows in their own settings, and nothing the user cannot clear also keeps them off), or 'unsupported_runtime' (this Claude Code process is not running on Bun, the runtime its binary is built with, and workflow scripts run only there).

policy_kind.description: policy_denied: the verdict — 'org_denied' (the organization's policy turns the feature off) or 'latched' (a HIPAA-regulated organization signed in earlier in this process; restarting clears it).

remedy.description: @internal The fix a host can offer for a tool result, stamped from structured producer state (never parsed from the result text). Kinds: mcp_needs_auth, mcp_disabled, mcp_required_missing, auth_expired, auth_overridden, auth_missing_scope, design_needs_authorization, sandbox_violation, outside_reads_blocked, memory_paused, feature_disabled, policy_denied, spawn_arg_limit (the command's exec image exceeded the OS argument limit), staged_for_review (a settings-file write held for the machine owner's review). New kinds are additive; treat an unknown kind as absent.

tool_result_meta.description: @internal Display metadata for this message's tool_result blocks, keyed by tool_use_id. non_execution_kind is the harness-stamped reason an is_error:true result did not carry the tool's own execution output (user-rejected / permission-rule / automode-* / interrupted / cancelled); absent means the tool ran to completion. remedy is the fix a host can offer for what the result reports (see SDKToolResultRemedy). An entry may carry a remedy alone, on a result that did run (a staged write, a sandbox violation on exit 0), so whether a call ran is read from non_execution_kind, never from an entry's presence. On a subagent's messages (parent_tool_use_id set), entries carry only permission_decision, so those messages do not say whether a call ran. permission_decision is how the call's permission check ended, as Claude Code's claude_code.tool.blocked_on_user trace span reports it. decision is accept, reject or cancelled. source names what decided: config, classifier, hook, user_temporary, user_permanent, user_reject, user_abort, or invalid_input, permission_updated_input_invalid or server_fallback_tombstone when bad input or the server ended the wait. Which label a rule gets depends on the session: in SDK sessions a rule for this session or in the user's own settings reports user_temporary, user_permanent or user_reject and other rules report config, while interactive sessions report every rule as config. reason_type is the kind of reason the check gave when it decided by itself, such as 'rule' whenever a rule decided, or 'classifier' for an auto-mode allow, which reports source config. reason_type is absent when a person or the SDK host answered the question, when the check's outcome was still a question, and for user_abort and the last three sources above. permission_decision is absent when the call ended before its permission check, and on some results built apart from the call's own run, such as a plugin hook's refusal, a hook's rewrite of a denied result, or the result the tool executor writes for a queued call that a stop cancelled. user_feedback is the deny comment a human typed at a permission prompt (the local dialog or a bridge client's deny UI), before the CLI's reject-message framing — absent when the deny was resolved by a coordinator, channel relay, or hook rather than a human. A deny answered through the SDK control protocol (can_use_tool / --permission-prompt-tool) currently reports as 'permission-rule' with no user_feedback, because that wire carries no human-provenance signal. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content` — so it is not replayed to the model. Clients read this instead of string-matching the result prose.

name.description: Sender display name, normalized by the harness: Unicode control, format, surrogate, and line/paragraph-separator code points stripped (categories Cc/Cf/Cs/Zl/Zp — covers bidi controls, zero-width characters, and tag characters), trimmed, at most 64 code points (+ ellipsis, never splitting a surrogate pair).
